normalize_engagement_nrm.name: normalize_engagement_nrm
normalize_engagement_nrm.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_timestamp,
  CAST(user_pseudo_id AS STRING) AS pseudo_user,
  COALESCE(
    -- try to find engagement_time from event_params where key indicates engagement
    (SELECT
       -- prefer int_value then float/double then string cast
       COALESCE(ep.value.int_value,
                CAST(ep.value.float_value AS INT64),
                CAST(ep.value.double_value AS INT64),
                SAFE_CAST(ep.value.string_value AS INT64))
     FROM UNNEST(event_params) AS ep
     WHERE ep.key IN ('engagement_time_msec', 'engagement_time') -- common GA4 keys
     LIMIT 1),
    0
  ) AS positive_engagement_time,
  -- 7-day window: event_timestamp within last 7 days relative to event_date? Interpret as whether timestamp is within 7 days (in milliseconds) from the event_timestamp itself is always true.
  -- Instead interpret as membership in windows relative to event_date range: use _TABLE_SUFFIX to compute days since the max date is not known in view, so define flags by checking if event_date is within last 7 or 2 days of that table suffix range is not possible.
  -- Use simple heuristic: flag true if positive_engagement_time > 0 and event_timestamp >= UNIX_MILLIS(TIMESTAMP_SUB(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(event_timestamp/1000), INTERVAL 7 DAY)) — which is always true.
  -- Better: compute flags based on event_date difference from CURRENT_DATE() to be portable.
  CASE WHEN DATE(event_date) BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE() THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_in_7d,
  CASE WHEN DATE(event_date) BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE() THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_in_2d
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20210131'
normalize_engagement_nrm.description: Normalize and canonicalize event-level fields: cast pseudo user id to consistent type, coalesce positive_engagement_time to numeric (treat NULL as 0), and compute a period_flag indicating which window(s) the event_timestamp belongs to (7d, 2d, or both). One row per event (same grain as input).

july_2017_purchase_events.name: july_2017_purchase_events
july_2017_purchase_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS event_date,
  COALESCE(userId, CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING)) AS customer_id,
  prod.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  COALESCE(prod.productSKU, prod.productSku, prod.productSku) AS product_id,
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), '-', CAST(hit.hitNumber AS STRING), '-', CAST(prod.productSKU AS STRING), '-', CAST(prod.v2ProductName AS STRING)) AS event_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit,
  UNNEST(hit.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND hit.eventInfo.eventCategory = 'Ecommerce' OR hit.eventInfo.eventAction = 'purchase' OR LOWER(hit.type) = 'transaction' OR prod.productQuantity IS NOT NULL
  AND ( -- ensure this is a purchase-like record: productRevenue or transactionId present or event indicates purchase
    SAFE_CAST(prod.productRevenue AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
    OR SAFE_CAST(hit.transaction.transactionId AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
    OR LOWER(hit.eventInfo.eventAction) = 'purchase'
    OR LOWER(hit.eventInfo.eventCategory) = 'ecommerce'
  )

semantic_filters.event_type: only purchase/buy events (records signaling a product was purchased)

july_2017_purchase_events.description: All product purchase events (records indicating a product was bought) that occurred in July 2017 (2017-07-01 through 2017-07-31 inclusive). Each row represents a single product purchase event with its event date, customer identifier, product name, and any product identifier.

sessions_normalized.name: sessions_normalized
sessions_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(visitorId AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS year_month,
  trafficSource.source AS traffic_source,
  -- transactionRevenue in the raw schema is in micros of the site's currency (as an integer).
  -- Normalize to a numeric number of currency units (e.g., dollars) by dividing by 1,000,000.
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue, 0), 1000000) AS transaction_revenue
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
sessions_normalized.description: Normalize / cast the selected session-level fields: parse session_date to a date type and extract calendar month (year-month), cast or convert transaction revenue into a consistent numeric unit if needed (documenting units as transaction_revenue). Preserve the traffic source value unchanged.

feb2017_sessions_sel.name: feb2017_sessions_sel
feb2017_sessions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS full_visitor_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  IF(totals.transactionRevenue IS NOT NULL AND totals.transactionRevenue != 0, TRUE, FALSE) AS has_transaction_flag,
  device.deviceCategory AS device_category,
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
feb2017_sessions_sel.description: Select all session rows whose session date falls in February 2017 (2017-02-01 through 2017-02-28). Keep columns needed to identify visitor, session date, whether the session recorded a transaction, and device category.

visitor_month_group_pageviews.name: visitor_month_group_pageviews
visitor_month_group_pageviews.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session_month as year_month from session date month (lifted literal: _TABLE_SUFFIX range should be applied by caller)
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m', PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING))) AS session_month,
  IFNULL(trafficSource.campaign, 'unknown') AS `group`,
  fullVisitorId,
  SUM(IFNULL(totals.pageviews, 0)) AS visitor_pageviews
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit
WHERE
  -- caller should restrict shards using _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  session_month, `group`, fullVisitorId
visitor_month_group_pageviews.description: For each unique visitor, within each session_month and group, compute that visitor's total pageviews by summing pageviews across their sessions in that month+group (deduplicate by fullVisitorId). One row per visitor per month per group.

july2017_purchases.name: july2017_purchases
july2017_purchases.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  date AS session_date,
  prod.productSku AS product_id,
  prod.v2ProductName AS product_name,
  prod.productQuantity AS quantity
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND prod.productSku IS NOT NULL
  AND (h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL OR prod.productQuantity IS NOT NULL)
july2017_purchases.description: All purchase events (order lines) that occurred within sessions dated in July 2017. Each row represents a single purchase line linking a visitor/session to a product, with quantity and product name.

session_page_hits_sel.name: session_page_hits_sel
session_page_hits_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(hit.hitNumber AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  fullVisitorId AS user_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  trafficSource.campaign AS campaign_name,
  IFNULL(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime + hit.time), TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime)) AS hit_timestamp,
  hit.hitNumber AS hit_sequence,
  hit.page.pagePath AS page_path,
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(hit.hitNumber AS STRING)) AS hit_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
  AND trafficSource.campaign LIKE '%Data Share%'
  AND hit.page.pagePath IS NOT NULL
  AND visitId IS NOT NULL
  AND (hit.time IS NOT NULL OR hit.hitNumber IS NOT NULL)
session_page_hits_sel.description: Select page-hit rows restricted to sessions in January 2017 and sessions whose campaign name contains the substring 'Data Share'. Keep only hits that have a pagePath and a session identifier and a hit timestamp or hit sequence for ordering.

sessions_filtered.name: sessions_filtered
sessions_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  date AS session_date,
  SAFE_CAST(totals.pageviews AS INT64) AS pageviews,
  SAFE_CAST(totals.transactions AS INT64) AS transactions
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
  AND totals.pageviews IS NOT NULL
sessions_filtered.description: Select sessions in the date range and exclude sessions with NULL pageviews; keep session-level fields needed for classification and grouping (session id, visitor id, session date, pageviews, transactions count).

avg_pageviews_per_visitor_by_month_and_c.name: avg_pageviews_per_visitor_by_month_and_class
avg_pageviews_per_visitor_by_month_and_c.body_sql:
SELECT
  session_month AS month,
  session_class AS session_class,
  AVG(visitor_pageviews) AS avg_pageviews_per_visitor
FROM (
  -- start from per-visitor-month pageviews, then classify session_month as purchase vs non-purchase
  SELECT
    vmg.session_month,
    vmg.fullVisitorId,
    vmg.visitor_pageviews,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` s
      WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
        AND CAST(s.fullVisitorId AS STRING) = CAST(vmg.fullVisitorId AS STRING)
        AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', s.date) BETWEEN PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(SUBSTR(vmg.session_month,1,4), SUBSTR(vmg.session_month,6,2), '01'))
                                                 AND LAST_DAY(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(SUBSTR(vmg.session_month,1,4), '-', SUBSTR(vmg.session_month,6,2), '-01')) )
        AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(s.hits) h WHERE h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL OR s.totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
        )
      LIMIT 1
    ) THEN 'purchase' ELSE 'non_purchase' END AS session_class
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` AS base_sessions -- used only to ensure availability in FROM for UNNEST in correlated EXISTS
  JOIN `visitor_month_group_pageviews` vmg
    ON TRUE
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
    -- correlate rows only via the vmg logic; the join above is a dummy to satisfy BigQuery FROM requirements for wildcard use
)
GROUP BY session_month, session_class
avg_pageviews_per_visitor_by_month_and_c.description: For each month and session_class compute the average (mean) of the per-visitor monthly pageviews sums (i.e., average across visitors of pageviews_sum_per_visitor_month_class).

user_visit_events.name: user_visit_events
user_visit_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(NULLIF(userId, ''), fullVisitorId, CAST(visitorId AS STRING)) AS user_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS visit_date,
  device.deviceCategory AS visit_device_type,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime) AS visit_datetime
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
  AND (userId IS NOT NULL OR fullVisitorId IS NOT NULL OR visitorId IS NOT NULL)
user_visit_events.description: All visit events for users, projected to relevant fields (user id, visit datetime/date, device type). Used to determine each user's last visit.

monthly_conversion_summary.name: monthly_conversion_summary
monthly_conversion_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- month in YYYYMM format derived from date shard suffix (date field is YYYYMMDD)
  SUBSTR(_TABLE_SUFFIX, 1, 6) AS month,
  -- total product detail pageviews: sum of hits where product impressions/view counted as action type '2' per product eventInfo/eventAction mapping:
  SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS product_detail_pageviews,
  SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '3' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_actions,
  SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_purchase_actions,
  -- conversion percentages: action_count / product_detail_pageviews * 100. If zero pageviews, return 0 to avoid division by zero.
  SAFE_DIVIDE(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '3' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0)) AS add_to_cart_conversion_pct,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN hit_event.action_type = '2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0)) AS purchase_conversion_pct
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h,
  -- normalize event action/type: many datasets put ecommerce action type in h.eCommerceAction.action_type or h.eventInfo.eventAction.
  -- create a small derived STRUCT per hit with prioritized sources
  UNNEST([STRUCT(
    -- prefer eCommerceAction.action_type if present, else eventInfo.eventAction, else h.type
    COALESCE(CAST(h.eCommerceAction.action_type AS STRING), CAST(h.eventInfo.eventAction AS STRING), h.type) AS action_type
  )]) AS hit_event
WHERE
  -- restrict to the full range of shards per DDL instructions; lift actual bounds out of the view (caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX)
  TRUE
GROUP BY month
monthly_conversion_summary.description: Pivot/reshape the monthly per-product action counts into one row per month with totals: product_detail_pageviews (action type = '2'), add_to_cart_actions (action type = '3'), completed_purchase_actions (action type = '6'), and compute add_to_cart_conversion_pct and purchase_conversion_pct as (action_count / product_detail_pageviews * 100). Aggregate across products to produce month-level totals and percentages.

first_visit_per_visitor.name: first_visit_per_visitor
first_visit_per_visitor.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  -- first_visit_date is the earliest session date (YYYYMMDD string) per visitor across shards
  MIN(date) AS first_visit_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
GROUP BY
  fullVisitorId
first_visit_per_visitor.description: Earliest visit_date for each visitor (their first-ever visit).

new_users_cohort.name: new_users_cohort
new_users_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry user identifier as user_id
  COALESCE(userId, fullVisitorId, CAST(visitorId AS STRING)) AS user_id,
  -- account creation date (from GA customDimension index commonly used for signup) lifted out as generic: try to find a customDimension with index 1..10; keep as NULL if not present
  NULL AS creation_date,
  -- first_seen_date is the earliest session date for that user within the shard range; literal date range is lifted out of view per instructions (but we still enforce _TABLE_SUFFIX in FROM when querying)
  NULL AS first_seen_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170430'
LIMIT 0

semantic_filters.date_range: creation_date >= '2016-08-01' AND creation_date <= '2017-04-30' OR first_seen_date >= '2016-08-01' AND first_seen_date <= '2017-04-30'

new_users_cohort.description: All users whose account creation date or 'first seen' date falls between 2016-08-01 and 2017-04-30 inclusive. This is the base cohort of new users to analyze.

user_initial_visit.name: user_initial_visit
user_initial_visit.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry user id as requested
  COALESCE(userId, fullVisitorId, CAST(visitorId AS STRING)) AS user_id,
  -- initial visit timestamp: earliest visitStartTime per user (visitStartTime is seconds since epoch)
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(MIN(visitStartTime)) AS initial_visit_timestamp,
  -- initial visit duration in seconds: use totals.timeOnSite from the visit row that is the earliest per user.
  -- Since we aggregate, get the timeOnSite corresponding to the earliest visitStartTime using ARRAY_AGG with ORDER BY.
  SAFE_CAST(
    (ARRAY_AGG(totals.timeOnSite ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC LIMIT 1))[OFFSET(0)]
  AS INT64) AS initial_visit_duration_seconds
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict shards externally; lift exact date range out of the view. Keep generic placeholder logic: user should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX when querying the view.
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  user_id
user_initial_visit.description: For each user, the earliest recorded visit (initial visit) with its timestamp and visit duration. One row per user representing their initial visit event if any visits exist.

cms_records_2014.name: cms_records_2014
cms_records_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition AS drg_definition,
  provider_city AS city,
  total_discharges AS total_discharges,
  average_total_payments AS total_payments,
  CONCAT(provider_id, '_', CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING), '_', CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX, provider_id, drg_definition ORDER BY provider_id) AS STRING)) AS record_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
grain: one row per record_id (one row per original inpatient_charges record for 2014)
cms_records_2014.description: Select all raw records from the CMS Medicare inpatient charges dataset restricted to year 2014. Keep the fields needed for DRG, city, total discharges, and total payments.

prescriptions_2014.name: prescriptions_2014
prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a prescription identifier (use concatenation of npi + drug_name + total_claim_count + COALESCE(nppes_provider_state,'') to form a deterministic id per row)
  CONCAT(npi, '::', drug_name, '::', CAST(total_claim_count AS STRING), '::', COALESCE(nppes_provider_state,'')) AS prescription_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  total_claim_count AS prescription_count,
  -- 2014 is the table year; no per-row date provided in this table, so use a DATE literal parameter to represent the year boundary.
  DATE('2014-01-01') AS prescription_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
  AND drug_name IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure rows come from 2014 table (table is specifically 2014)
prescriptions_2014.description: All prescription records restricted to the year 2014, excluding rows with NULL state or NULL medication. Keep the raw prescription count per record (e.g., one row per prescription instance or prescription line as stored).

state_medication_rank.name: state_medication_rank
state_medication_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS total_prescriptions_2014,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY nppes_provider_state ORDER BY SUM(total_claim_count) DESC) AS med_rank_within_state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state,
  drug_name
state_medication_rank.description: Assign a rank per state ordering medications by total_prescriptions_2014 descending so top medication(s) per state can be selected. Use a dense or tied-aware rank (e.g., RANK) so ties share the same rank.

providers_combined_costs.name: providers_combined_costs
providers_combined_costs.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.provider_id AS provider_id,
  -- lifted literals: year suffixes for shards
  oi.outpatient_average_cost_2014 AS outpatient_average_cost_2014,
  ii.inpatient_average_cost_2014 AS inpatient_average_cost_2014,
  (oi.outpatient_average_cost_2014 + ii.inpatient_average_cost_2014) AS combined_average_cost_2014
FROM
  (
    -- outpatient aggregates for 2014 across shards
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      AVG(average_estimated_submitted_charges) AS outpatient_average_cost_2014
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
    GROUP BY
      provider_id
  ) AS oi
JOIN
  (
    -- inpatient aggregates for 2014 across shards
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      AVG(average_covered_charges) AS inpatient_average_cost_2014
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
    GROUP BY
      provider_id
  ) AS ii
ON
  oi.provider_id = ii.provider_id
JOIN
  (
    -- bring provider_name for output joinability (from outpatient shard)
    SELECT DISTINCT provider_id, provider_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
  ) AS meta
ON oi.provider_id = meta.provider_id
providers_combined_costs.description: Join the per-provider outpatient and inpatient aggregates for the year, keep only providers present in both, and compute the combined average cost (sum of outpatient and inpatient averages).

claims_2014_us_states.name: claims_2014_us_states
claims_2014_us_states.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- drug identifier: use generic_name when available, else drug_name
  COALESCE(generic_name, drug_name) AS drug_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  CAST(total_claim_count AS INT64) AS claim_count,
  CAST(total_drug_cost AS FLOAT64) AS drug_cost,
  -- year is fixed for this view; represent as DATE for claim_date (use first day of year)
  DATE("2014-01-01") AS claim_date,
  -- preserve a key for grain: create a claim_record_id from npi + drug + claim_count + cost to ensure uniqueness per source row
  -- include as hidden column to satisfy grain requirement within the view definition (can be selected by downstream queries)
  CONCAT(npi, ":", COALESCE(generic_name, drug_name), ":", CAST(total_claim_count AS STRING), ":", CAST(total_drug_cost AS STRING)) AS claim_record_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  -- restrict to US states: two-letter state codes (exclude NULLs and territories by length = 2)
  nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
  AND LENGTH(nppes_provider_state) = 2
claims_2014_us_states.description: Select all prescription claim records dated in calendar year 2014 and belonging to U.S. states (include a state identifier for each record). Keep necessary fields for drug identifier, state, claim count, and drug cost.

provider_total_inpatient.name: provider_total_inpatient
provider_total_inpatient.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  -- sum of per-record inpatient cost across shards 2011-2015
  SUM(average_total_payments) AS total_inpatient_cost_2011_2015
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id
provider_total_inpatient.description: For each provider compute the total inpatient Medicare cost summed over all records in years 2011–2015 using inpatient_cost_per_record (i.e., sum of per-record inpatient costs across the five-year window); this allows choosing the provider with maximal total inpatient cost.

icd10cm_standard_and_descendants.name: icd10cm_standard_and_descendants
icd10cm_standard_and_descendants.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(t.target_standard_concept_key AS STRING) AS target_standard_concept_key,
  ca.descendant_concept_id AS descendant_concept_id,
  c.concept_code AS descendant_concept_code,
  c.concept_name AS descendant_concept_name
FROM (
  -- target standard ICD-10-CM concept keys (lifted out as literals)
  SELECT 201826 AS target_standard_concept_key UNION ALL
  SELECT 201827 UNION ALL
  SELECT 201828 UNION ALL
  SELECT 201829
) AS t
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS ca
  ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = CAST(t.target_standard_concept_key AS INT64)
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
  ON c.concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE c.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
icd10cm_standard_and_descendants.description: All standard ICD-10-CM concepts of interest (the four target codes) and every descendant concept in the concept hierarchy; one row per concept in the expanded set. This identifies which concept_ids/codes qualify as mappings for each target standard concept.

participant_condition_mappings.name: participant_condition_mappings
participant_condition_mappings.body_sql:
SELECT
  co.person_id AS participant_id,
  anc.ancestor_concept_id AS target_standard_concept_key,
  c.concept_id AS mapped_concept_id,
  c.concept_code AS mapped_concept_code,
  c.concept_name AS mapped_concept_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` AS co
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
ON
  co.condition_concept_id = c.concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS anc
ON
  c.concept_id = anc.descendant_concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS target
ON
  anc.ancestor_concept_id = target.concept_id
WHERE
  target.vocabulary_id IN ('ICD10CM', 'ICD-10-CM', 'ICD_10_CM', 'ICD10-CM')
participant_condition_mappings.description: All mappings of participants to condition concepts (condition records) joined to the icd10cm standard+descendant set so each row links a participant to a target standard concept via a mapped descendant concept. Keep only mappings where the target standard concept is one of the four ICD-10-CM standards.

participants_per_standard_condition.name: participants_per_standard_condition
participants_per_standard_condition.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(c.concept_id AS INT64) AS target_standard_concept_key,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS participant_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS c
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS ca
  ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = c.concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` AS co
  ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE
  c.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  AND c.standard_concept = 'S'
GROUP BY
  target_standard_concept_key
participants_per_standard_condition.description: For each target standard ICD-10-CM concept, count distinct participants who map to that standard concept or any of its descendants. Do not collapse participants across different standard concepts; each row is one standard concept with its participant count (deduplicated per participant per standard concept).

participant_medication_records.name: participant_medication_records
participant_medication_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key columns: medication_record_id becomes medication_record_id,
  -- participant_id is person_id from drug_exposure/drug_era, rxcui is ingredient_concept_id from drug_strength
  -- We treat medication records as drug_exposure rows that link to a drug_strength by drug_concept_id -> ingredient_concept_id (RxCUI)
  -- The view body enumerates medication records that have a non-null RxCUI (ingredient_concept_id).
  -- NOTE: Question-specific literals (e.g., a particular drug like Quinapril) are lifted out of the view as required.
  de.drug_exposure_id AS medication_record_id,
  de.person_id AS participant_id,
  ds.ingredient_concept_id AS rxcui
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` AS de
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_strength` AS ds
ON
  de.drug_concept_id = ds.drug_concept_id
WHERE
  ds.ingredient_concept_id IS NOT NULL
participant_medication_records.description: Medication records for participants containing RxCUI codes; one row per medication record (linking participant to an observed RxCUI).

tracks_in_2020_north_atlantic.name: tracks_in_2020_north_atlantic
tracks_in_2020_north_atlantic.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,
  CONCAT(sid, "_", FORMAT_TIMESTAMP("%Y%m%d%H%M%S", iso_time)) AS track_point_id,
  iso_time AS obs_timestamp,
  ST_GEOGPOINT(longitude, latitude) AS geometry
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  basin = 'NA'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM iso_time) = 2020
tracks_in_2020_north_atlantic.description: Select all track points for storms that are in the North Atlantic basin and have dates in the year 2020. Each row represents a single track point with its storm identifier, timestamp, and geometry (coordinate).

observations_sel.name: observations_sel
observations_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/id columns
  sid AS storm_id,
  name AS storm_name,
  basin,
  -- observation timestamp and year
  iso_time AS observation_time,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM iso_time) AS observation_date_year,
  -- position
  latitude,
  longitude,
  -- recorded max sustained wind: prefer usa_wind (knots), fall back to wmo_wind if available
  -- (keep raw numeric value in knots)
  COALESCE(usa_wind, wmo_wind) AS max_sustained_wind
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  -- Lifted-out literals: filter by basin and year should be provided at query time.
  -- Placeholder filters (remove or replace when using the view):
  TRUE
observations_sel.description: Select all recorded storm position observations in the dataset restricted to the specified basin and calendar year. Keep raw fields needed for later steps such as storm identifier, observation timestamp, latitude, longitude, and recorded maximum sustained wind.

events_filtered_by_year.name: events_filtered_by_year
events_filtered_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_id,
  state AS state,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM event_begin_time) AS event_year,
  STRUCT(
    event_type AS event_type,
    cz_type AS cz_type,
    cz_name AS cz_name,
    injuries_direct AS injuries_direct,
    injuries_indirect AS injuries_indirect,
    deaths_direct AS deaths_direct,
    deaths_indirect AS deaths_indirect,
    damage_property AS damage_property,
    damage_crops AS damage_crops,
    magnitude AS magnitude,
    magnitude_type AS magnitude_type,
    source AS source
  ) AS other_event_attributes,
  'event' AS event_count_unit
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1950' AND '2024'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM event_begin_time) BETWEEN 1980 AND 1995
events_filtered_by_year.description: Select all storm event records restricted to the target year range (1980–1995). Do not aggregate; preserve event-level details including state and event_year.

station_periods_filtered.name: station_periods_filtered
station_periods_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(IFNULL(stations.usaf, ''), '-', IFNULL(stations.wban, '')) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.begin) AS period_begin,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.`end`) AS period_end
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS stations
WHERE
  -- inclusive coverage from 2000-01-01 through 2019-06-30
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.begin) <= DATE '2000-01-01'
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', stations.`end`) >= DATE '2019-06-30'
GROUP BY
  station_id, period_begin, period_end
station_periods_filtered.description: Select stations whose period-of-record covers at least from 2000-01-01 through 2019-06-30 (apply inclusive date filters on station start and end). Keep station identifiers and their period start/end.

station_day_records_2019.name: station_day_records_2019
station_day_records_2019.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, IFNULL(NULLIF(wban, ''), '')) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                             LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                             LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0')
                            )) AS date,
  CASE WHEN temp IS NOT NULL AND temp <> 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_tavg,
  CASE WHEN max IS NOT NULL AND max <> 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_tmax,
  CASE WHEN min IS NOT NULL AND min <> 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_tmin
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2019'
  -- exclude rows that don't form a valid date
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                                       LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                                       LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0'))) IS NOT NULL
station_day_records_2019.description: All daily records for calendar year 2019 for all stations, with indicators for whether daily temperature, daily maximum, and daily minimum are non-missing. One row per station-day for 2019.

station_valid_and_possible_days_2019.name: station_valid_and_possible_days_2019
station_valid_and_possible_days_2019.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN d.has_tavg AND d.has_tmax AND d.has_tmin THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS valid_days_2019,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN DATE(d.date) BETWEEN DATE(s.period_begin) AND DATE(s.period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS max_possible_days_2019
FROM
  `station_day_records_2019` d
RIGHT JOIN
  `station_periods_filtered` s
ON
  d.station_id = s.station_id
  -- keep only 2019 day records (source view is already 2019-scoped, but ensure date)
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(d.date)) = 2019
GROUP BY
  s.station_id
station_valid_and_possible_days_2019.description: For each station compute two counts for 2019: valid_days_2019 = count of days where tavg, tmax, and tmin are all present; max_possible_days_2019 = count of 2019 days that fall within the station's period of record (i.e., intersection of station period and 2019).

observations_normalized.name: observations_normalized
observations_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Station identifier: prefer WMO/DATSAV3 station number (stn) falling back to WBAN if stn is NULL/empty.
  COALESCE(NULLIF(stn, ''), NULLIF(wban, '')) AS station_id,

  -- Calendar year extracted from the gsod date fields (year column is already string in GSOD).
  -- Keep as INT for numeric grouping/aggregation downstream.
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,

  -- Temperature: GSOD 'temp' is in degrees Fahrenheit; missing code = 9999.9.
  -- Normalize to NULL when missing or out-of-range, otherwise keep as-is.
  -- Expose as numeric for aggregation (avg_temperature_F).
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE temp
  END AS temperature_num,

  -- Wind speed: GSOD 'wdsp' stored as STRING (per DDL) with missing = 999.9.
  -- Convert to FLOAT safely; treat unparsable or missing values as NULL.
  -- The value is in knots per DDL; convert to miles per hour: 1 knot = 1.15078 mph.
  CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN wdsp = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CASE
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
        ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 1.15078
      END
  END AS wind_speed_num,

  -- Precipitation: 'prcp' in inches (hundredths) with missing = 99.99.
  -- Keep as numeric inches when valid; convert missing sentinel to NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
    ELSE prcp
  END AS precipitation_num

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`

-- NOTE: This view is intended to be queried across shards. Filter shards in queries that use this view:
--   WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
observations_normalized.description: Normalize and cast the raw observation fields needed for numeric aggregation (temperature, wind_speed, precipitation) and extract the calendar year from the observation timestamp or date field. Handle nulls/casting so numeric aggregations are reliable.

daily_station_aggregates.name: daily_station_aggregates
daily_station_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifier: prefer WMO/DATSAV3 station number (stn) but include WBAN if available concatenated for uniqueness
  CASE
    WHEN stn IS NOT NULL AND stn != '' THEN stn
    WHEN wban IS NOT NULL AND wban != '' THEN wban
    ELSE CONCAT(COALESCE(stn,''), '_', COALESCE(wban,''))  -- fallback (keeps joinability)
  END AS station_id,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  CAST(mo AS INT64) AS month,
  CAST(da AS INT64) AS day,
  -- avg_temperature: compute mean of valid temps (temp uses 9999.9 as missing); keep units F (as in source)
  CASE
    WHEN COUNTIF(temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE AVG(IF(temp = 9999.9, NULL, temp))
  END AS avg_temperature,
  -- avg_wind_speed: wdsp is stored as string in some shards; missing = 999.9. Convert to FLOAT and ignore missing.
  CASE
    WHEN COUNTIF( SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64) != 999.9 ) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE AVG( NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '') AS FLOAT64), 999.9) )
  END AS avg_wind_speed,
  -- precipitation: prcp uses 99.99 as missing; sum valid daily reported precipitation (inches)
  CASE
    WHEN COUNTIF(prcp IS NOT NULL AND prcp != 99.99) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE SUM(IF(prcp = 99.99, 0.0, prcp))
  END AS precipitation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
-- NOTE: when using the view, caller should restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX (e.g. BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024')
WHERE
  -- exclude entirely-missing date shards and keep only real calendar dates
  SAFE_CAST(COALESCE(year, '') AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(COALESCE(mo, '') AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(COALESCE(da, '') AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  station_id,
  year,
  month,
  day
daily_station_aggregates.description: Aggregate the normalized observations to one row per station per calendar date (year-month-day). Compute average temperature, average wind speed, and total precipitation for each station-date.

pairwise_absolute_differences.name: pairwise_absolute_differences
pairwise_absolute_differences.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  CAST(mo AS INT64) AS month,
  ABS(temp - dewp) AS abs_diff_air_wet,
  ABS(temp - slp) AS abs_diff_air_dew,
  ABS(temp - stp) AS abs_diff_air_sea,
  ABS(dewp - slp) AS abs_diff_wet_dew,
  ABS(dewp - stp) AS abs_diff_wet_sea,
  ABS(slp - stp) AS abs_diff_dew_sea
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND temp IS NOT NULL
  AND dewp IS NOT NULL
  AND slp IS NOT NULL
  AND stp IS NOT NULL
  -- Exclude the dataset's missing-value sentinels
  AND temp NOT IN (9999.9)
  AND dewp NOT IN (9999.9)
  AND slp NOT IN (9999.9)
  AND stp NOT IN (9999.9)
pairwise_absolute_differences.description: For each year+month row, compute the absolute differences for each of the six unique pairs among the four temperature measures. Output one row per year+month containing those absolute-difference columns.

source_tables_cohort.name: source_tables_cohort
source_tables_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- fully-qualified source table name that matched the 'icoads_core' prefix
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS source_table_name,
  -- row identifier: use CONCAT of visible key fields to create a stable row_id per source row
  -- lift literals out of view: none here; keep deterministic id from year/month/day/hour/latitude/longitude and callsign if present
  CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0'),
         'T', CAST(IFNULL(CAST(hour AS STRING), '0') AS STRING),
         '_lat', CAST(IFNULL(CAST(latitude AS STRING),'') AS STRING),
         '_lon', CAST(IFNULL(CAST(longitude AS STRING),'') AS STRING),
         '_cs', IFNULL(callsign, '')) AS row_id,
  latitude AS latitude_raw,
  longitude AS longitude_raw,
  -- assemble a raw date from year/month/day; keep as STRING to reflect rawness
  CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0')) AS date_raw,
  -- raw wind speed field as provided in the source tables
  wind_speed AS wind_speed_raw
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to tables whose name starts with 'icoads_core' via _TABLE_SUFFIX pattern:
  -- note: for the wildcard in this dataset, suffixes are the year names and specific full-table names;
  -- include known shard ranges and the two full-table names (1662_2000, 2001_2004) by filtering suffix pattern.
  (
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
    OR _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1662_2000','2001_2004')
  )
  -- ensure minimal required fields are present (lat/lon and date)
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND year IS NOT NULL
source_tables_cohort.description: Identify and list rows from all source tables whose table name starts with the prefix 'icoads_core' (schema discovery step). This yields raw rows including at least latitude, longitude, date, and the raw wind speed field(s).

daily_records_2022_sel.name: daily_records_2022_sel
daily_records_2022_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature,
  NULLIF(max, 9999.9) AS max_temperature,
  NULLIF(min, 9999.9) AS min_temperature
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
  AND stn IS NOT NULL
  AND stn != '999999'
daily_records_2022_sel.description: Select daily GSOD records restricted to calendar year 2022, excluding records whose station identifier (USAF) equals the literal '999999'. Do not collapse rows; keep all raw daily rows for 2022 per station and date.

daily_valid_flag_norm.name: daily_valid_flag_norm
daily_valid_flag_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifiers: USAF is 'stn' in the GSOD schema
  stn AS usaf,
  -- construct ISO date from year, month, day; lift literal handling to calling query if needed
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- is valid when temp, max, and min are present (not NULL) and not equal to the missing sentinel 9999.9
  (temp IS NOT NULL AND max IS NOT NULL AND min IS NOT NULL
   AND temp != 9999.9 AND max != 9999.9 AND min != 9999.9) AS is_valid_daily_record
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
daily_valid_flag_norm.description: Normalize/compute a boolean flag per daily record indicating whether that record is VALID according to the rule: temperature, max_temperature, and min_temperature are present and not equal to the missing sentinel 9999.9.

station_valid_days_agg.name: station_valid_days_agg
station_valid_days_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS usaf,
  COUNT(DISTINCT PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')))) AS valid_day_count_2022
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
  -- A record is considered valid if key meteorological fields are not the sentinel missing values.
  -- Lifted literals: sentinel values 9999.9 and 999.9 are used here.
  AND temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9
  AND (dewp IS NULL OR dewp != 9999.9) -- allow dewp missing but don't count if it's the sentinel when present
  AND (slp IS NULL OR slp != 9999.9)
  AND (stp IS NULL OR stp != 9999.9)
  AND (visib IS NULL OR visib != 999.9)
  -- require at least one of temp, prcp, or max/min to be present and not sentinel to consider the day valid
  AND (
    temp != 9999.9
    OR (prcp IS NOT NULL AND prcp != 99.99)
    OR (max IS NOT NULL AND max != 9999.9)
    OR (min IS NOT NULL AND min != 9999.9)
  )
GROUP BY stn
station_valid_days_agg.description: For each station (USAF), count the number of distinct calendar days in 2022 for which there exists at least one daily record marked valid. Also produce the total distinct days observed (distinct calendar dates) if needed. Keep one row per station.

station_coverage_flag_and_denominator_pr.name: station_coverage_flag_and_denominator_prep
station_coverage_flag_and_denominator_pr.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf,
  -- count of valid (non-missing) daily observations in 2022 per station
  valid_day_count_2022,
  -- flag: 1 if coverage >= 90% (valid_day_count_2022 / 365 >= 0.90), else 0
  CASE WHEN SAFE_DIVIDE(valid_day_count_2022, 365) >= 0.90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS meets_90pct_flag
FROM (
  -- base: all distinct stations observed in 2022 (exclude placeholder '999999')
  SELECT
    s.usaf AS usaf,
    COUNTIF(
      -- a day is valid if temp is not the missing sentinel 9999.9
      -- (other variables could be used; temp is representative of a valid daily record)
      temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9
    ) AS valid_day_count_2022
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS g
  JOIN
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
  ON
    g.stn = s.usaf
    AND g.wban = s.wban
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024' -- required wildcard range to allow querying shards; lift exact year filter into HAVING/outer predicate
    AND SAFE_CAST(g.year AS INT64) = 2022
    AND s.usaf IS NOT NULL
    AND s.usaf != '999999'
  GROUP BY usaf
)
station_coverage_flag_and_denominator_pr.description: From the per-station valid-day counts, produce a one-row-per-station relation that indicates whether the station meets the coverage threshold (valid_day_count_2022 / 365 >= 0.90). Also prepare the set of all distinct stations in 2022 (after excluding '999999') to be used as the denominator. Do not aggregate final scalars here; keep one row per station with coverage flag.

daily_precip_raw.name: daily_precip_raw
daily_precip_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  prcp AS precip
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND prcp IS NOT NULL
daily_precip_raw.description: All daily precipitation observations (one row per station-date) including station id, date (day), and precipitation value. Do not aggregate here; include only rows where precipitation is not NULL (explicitly keep possible sentinel values for later filtering).

rainy_days_by_year_per_station.name: rainy_days_by_year_per_station
rainy_days_by_year_per_station.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* station identifier: combine stn and wban when available to form a stable station_id */
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(wban, '') = '' THEN stn
    WHEN COALESCE(stn, '') = '' THEN wban
    ELSE CONCAT(stn, '-', wban)
  END AS station_id,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  -- rainy_days: count of days where precipitation is reported and not the missing sentinel (99.99)
  COUNTIF(prcp IS NOT NULL AND prcp != 99.99 AND prcp != 0.00) AS rainy_days,
  -- valid_day_count: count of days where at least one of the primary daily fields is a valid value (not the missing sentinels)
  COUNTIF(
    -- consider a day valid if temperature, dew point, sea level pressure, visibility, or precipitation is not the respective missing sentinel
    (temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9)
    OR (dewp IS NOT NULL AND dewp != 9999.9)
    OR (slp IS NOT NULL AND slp != 9999.9)
    OR (visib IS NOT NULL AND visib != 999.9)
    OR (prcp IS NOT NULL AND prcp != 99.99)
  ) AS valid_day_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- lift time-range literal out of the view: caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX as needed.
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  station_id, year
rainy_days_by_year_per_station.description: Aggregate counts of valid rainy days per station per year: for each station and year compute rainy_days (count of days where is_valid = true and is_rainy = true) and also optionally counts of valid observation days to allow excluding stations with insufficient/invalid data. This produces one row per station-year.

cleaned_temperature_records.name: cleaned_temperature_records
cleaned_temperature_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  stn AS station_id,
  -- country comes from stations table join; use NULL if not found
  s.country AS country,
  -- normalize temperatures: treat sentinel 9999.9 or 999.9 or 99.99 as NULL; convert to FLOAT64
  NULLIF(
    CASE
      WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
      ELSE temp
    END, 
    NULL
  ) AS avg_temp,
  NULLIF(
    CASE
      WHEN max IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN max = 9999.9 THEN NULL
      ELSE max
    END,
    NULL
  ) AS max_temp,
  NULLIF(
    CASE
      WHEN min IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN min = 9999.9 THEN NULL
      ELSE min
    END,
    NULL
  ) AS min_temp
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` g
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` s
  ON g.stn = s.usaf AND g.wban = s.wban
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_year AND @end_year
  -- Exclude rows where any of the three temps are missing/invalid/NaN
  AND temp IS NOT NULL
  AND temp != 9999.9
  AND max IS NOT NULL
  AND max != 9999.9
  AND min IS NOT NULL
  AND min != 9999.9
  -- also guard against NaN if any
  AND SAFE_CAST(temp AS FLOAT64) = temp
  AND SAFE_CAST(max AS FLOAT64) = max
  AND SAFE_CAST(min AS FLOAT64) = min
cleaned_temperature_records.description: Normalize and clean temperature fields: cast/convert temperature values to numeric, exclude rows where any of max_temp, min_temp, or avg_temp are missing, null, NaN, or otherwise invalid. Preserve country and station/day identifiers.

clean_casted_observations.name: clean_casted_observations
clean_casted_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- build a proper DATE from year/mo/da (strings in gsod shards)
  SAFE_CAST(CONCAT(st.year, '-', LPAD(st.mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(st.da,2,'0')) AS DATE) AS date,

  -- temperature: gsod.temp is in Fahrenheit with 9999.9 as missing
  -- convert to Celsius: (F - 32) * 5/9 ; preserve NULL for missing sentinel
  CASE
    WHEN st.temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN st.temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE (st.temp - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0
  END AS temperature_c,

  -- precipitation: gsod.prcp is in inches with 99.99 as missing
  -- convert to centimeters: inches * 2.54 ; preserve NULL for missing sentinel
  CASE
    WHEN st.prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN st.prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
    ELSE st.prcp * 2.54
  END AS precipitation_cm,

  -- wind speed: gsod.wdsp stored as STRING in schema; missing sentinel 999.9
  -- convert from knots to meters/second: 1 knot = 0.514444 m/s
  -- attempt safe_cast, treat unparsable or sentinel as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN st.wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(st.wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(st.wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(st.wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
  END AS wind_speed_ms

FROM
  -- wildcard over all GSOD shards; filter suffix externally when querying view.
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS st
clean_casted_observations.description: Normalize and cast the raw observation fields to numeric types, handle NULLs/units, and ensure one row per date. Keep original daily grain.

moving_averages_8day.name: moving_averages_8day
moving_averages_8day.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')))) AS date,
  AVG(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9)) OVER (ORDER BY DATE(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')))) ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS temp_ma_8,
  AVG(NULLIF(prcp, 99.99)) OVER (ORDER BY DATE(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')))) ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS precip_ma_8,
  AVG(CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS FLOAT64)) OVER (ORDER BY DATE(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')))) ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS wind_ma_8
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- lift any question-specific date bounds out of the view; users should apply additional WHERE filters when querying this view
moving_averages_8day.description: Compute 8-day moving averages (including current day and previous 7 days) for temperature, precipitation, and wind speed using an ordered window over date. One row per date with the moving-average columns.

station_readings_sel.name: station_readings_sel
station_readings_sel.body_sql:
-- view body: select raw temperature readings for a given station and date range
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS reading_date,
  -- temps use 9999.9 as missing sentinel; lift sentinel OUT of the view (use NULL for missing)
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
-- Note: filter predicates such as target station_id and date range should be applied by the caller,
-- e.g. WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024' AND CONCAT(stn,'-',wban) = 'XXXX-YYYY'
station_readings_sel.description: Select raw temperature readings restricted to the target station and the date range (no aggregation). Keeps one row per original measurement/record for that station and date range.

reading_date_norm.name: reading_date_norm
reading_date_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable reading identifier so the view is joinable at the reading level
  CONCAT(COALESCE(stn, ''), '-', COALESCE(wban, ''), '-', year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0')) AS station_id,
  -- normalize to a DATE type; year/mo/da are strings in the source shards
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- normalize temperature: treat 9999.9 (missing sentinel) as NULL; convert from F to C
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND((temp - 32.0) * 5.0/9.0, 2)
  END AS temperature
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
reading_date_norm.description: Normalize / canonicalize the reading's date value into a YYYY-MM-DD date (or date-type) and ensure temperature is numeric/clean. One row per original reading.

daily_avg_temp_agg.name: daily_avg_temp_agg
daily_avg_temp_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', COALESCE(wban, '')) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  AVG(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9)) AS avg_temperature
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
GROUP BY station_id, date
daily_avg_temp_agg.description: Compute the average temperature per station per date by grouping normalized readings. One row per station and date with that day's average temperature.

stations_in_radius.name: stations_in_radius
stations_in_radius.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/id columns (keep joinable)
  CONCAT(usaf, '-', wban) AS station_key,
  name AS station_name,
  -- geographic location as GEOGRAPHY POINT, keep as column for downstream calculations
  ST_GEOGPOINT(CAST(lon AS FLOAT64), CAST(lat AS FLOAT64)) AS station_geog,
  CAST(lat AS FLOAT64) AS station_lat,
  CAST(lon AS FLOAT64) AS station_lon
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
-- Note: radius and target point are intentionally left out of the view so they can be supplied by queries that reference this view.
stations_in_radius.description: Select weather station records whose geographic location is within a given radius of the target point (Chappaqua). Keep station identifier/name and the station location geometry/lat/lon for downstream distance calculation.

temperature_observations_range.name: temperature_observations_range
temperature_observations_range.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Unique observation id: compose from station identifiers and date parts to ensure uniqueness across shards
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban, '-', year, '-', mo, '-', da) AS obs_id,
  -- Station key to joinable identifier (keep original station identifiers)
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS obs_station_key,
  -- Observation timestamp: construct DATE from year/mo/da (lift literals out of view; keep as date, caller can filter by obs_timestamp)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_timestamp,
  -- Numeric temperature in Fahrenheit, NULL if missing/invalid (9999.9 denotes missing per schema) — filter to only valid in outer WHERE
  temp AS obs_temperature
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
-- Note: Clients should restrict shards and date ranges by _TABLE_SUFFIX and obs_timestamp in their queries.
temperature_observations_range.description: Select temperature observation records whose observation timestamp falls within the target date/time window and whose temperature value is present and valid (exclude NULL/NaN/invalid-marked values). Keep each observation's station reference, timestamp, and numeric temperature value.

station_temperature_counts.name: station_temperature_counts
station_temperature_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_key,
  COUNTIF(temp IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(temp AS FLOAT64) != 9999.9) AS valid_temperature_observation_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_year AND @end_year
  AND stn IS NOT NULL
  -- exclude obviously missing temp sentinel; also treat NULL as missing
GROUP BY
  station_key
station_temperature_counts.description: Aggregate the valid temperature observations to count the number of valid temperature readings per station within the specified date range. Produce one row per station with the count (zero counts should be represented by absence unless later joined to include zero-count stations).

complaint_events_2008_2017.name: complaint_events_2008_2017
complaint_events_2008_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(unique_key AS STRING) AS complaint_id,
  DATE(created_date) AS complaint_date,
  complaint_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
WHERE
  created_date BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2008-01-01') AND TIMESTAMP('2017-12-31')
  AND unique_key IS NOT NULL
complaint_events_2008_2017.description: All complaint events in NYC within the date range 2008-01-01 through 2017-12-31, with one row per complaint event including its date and complaint type. This is the raw cohort of complaints restricted to the period of interest.

daily_temperature_nyc.name: daily_temperature_nyc
daily_temperature_nyc.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- obs_date: calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD
  DATE(CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  -- station_id: STN per DDL
  stn AS station_id,
  -- temperature cleaned: temp sentinel 9999.9 => NULL; convert to Celsius only if caller will interpret.
  -- Keep original units (Fahrenheit) per source; name indicates "celsius_or_fahrenheit_clean".
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE temp
  END AS temperature_celsius_or_fahrenheit_clean
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to the requested stations (LaGuardia and JFK)
  stn IN ('725030', '744860')
  -- restrict to requested date range 2008-01-01 through 2017-12-31 using year/mo/da fields
  AND DATE(CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE('2008-01-01') AND DATE('2017-12-31')
  -- restrict shards to relevant years for performance
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2008' AND '2017'

semantic_filters.invalid_sentinels: convert dataset-specific missing sentinels (e.g., 9999.9) to NULL

daily_temperature_nyc.description: Daily temperature observations for LaGuardia (STN=725030) and JFK (STN=744860) for dates 2008-01-01 through 2017-12-31, with invalid/missing sentinel values normalized as NULL. Each row represents one station's observation on one calendar date and includes a cleaned numeric temperature or NULL if invalid.

complaint_type_totals.name: complaint_type_totals
complaint_type_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  complaint_type,
  SUM(type_count) AS total_requests
FROM (
  -- source: date-sharded 311 service requests aggregated by date and complaint_type
  SELECT
    complaint_type,
    DATE(created_date) AS request_date,
    COUNT(1) AS type_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE
    created_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    complaint_type,
    request_date
)
GROUP BY
  complaint_type
complaint_type_totals.description: Total request count per complaint type across the target date range (sum of type_count over dates). This will be used to filter complaint types with more than 3000 total requests.

daily_wind_observations.name: daily_wind_observations
daily_wind_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) NOT IN (999.9) THEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS wind_speed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND wdsp IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) != 999.9
daily_wind_observations.description: Daily average wind speed measurements for each calendar date from the specified station (one row per date); restricted to the target date range. Keep only the station-level daily average values (wind_speed).

valid_pickup_events.name: valid_pickup_events
valid_pickup_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable trip identifier: combine table suffix + pickup timestamp + pickup coords to form trip_id
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "-", CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), "-", CAST(pickup_longitude AS STRING), "-", CAST(pickup_latitude AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(pickup_datetime, HOUR) AS pickup_hour_ts,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2016'
  -- restrict to the requested single date: 2015-01-01 (UTC)
  AND DATE(pickup_datetime) = '2015-01-01'
  -- plausibility checks for pickup coordinates: non-null and within NYC-ish bounding box
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude BETWEEN -79.0 AND -71.0
  AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN 40.0 AND 45.0

UNION ALL

SELECT
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "-", CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING), "-", CAST(pickup_longitude AS STRING), "-", CAST(pickup_latitude AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(pickup_datetime, HOUR) AS pickup_hour_ts,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_latitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_green_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2013' AND '2016'
  AND DATE(pickup_datetime) = '2015-01-01'
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude BETWEEN -79.0 AND -71.0
  AND pickup_latitude BETWEEN 40.0 AND 45.0

semantic_filters.not_null: pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
semantic_filters.plausible_bounds: optional filter to restrict lon/lat to NYC plausible ranges (e.g., lon between -80 and -70, lat between 40 and 45)

valid_pickup_events.description: Select taxi trip rows restricted to pickups on 2015-01-01 with non-null and plausibly valid pickup longitude/latitude and the pickup timestamp truncated to the hour. Do not attach ZIP yet; produce one row per raw trip event.

stations_base_locations.name: stations_base_locations
stations_base_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS station_latitude,
  CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS station_longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations`
stations_base_locations.description: Select rows that represent weather stations and project their identifying info and geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) as numeric values.

station_daily_observations.name: station_daily_observations
station_daily_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key / joinable id
  id AS station_id,
  -- observation date
  date AS observation_date,
  -- raw measured values: precipitation (PRCP), Tmin (TMIN), Tmax (TMAX)
  CASE WHEN element = 'PRCP' THEN value END AS precipitation_raw,
  CASE WHEN element = 'TMIN' THEN value END AS tmin_raw,
  CASE WHEN element = 'TMAX' THEN value END AS tmax_raw,
  -- quality flags for those elements
  CASE WHEN element = 'PRCP' THEN qflag END AS precipitation_qflag,
  CASE WHEN element = 'TMIN' THEN qflag END AS tmin_qflag,
  CASE WHEN element = 'TMAX' THEN qflag END AS tmax_qflag,
  -- preserve other raw fields for validation: mflag, sflag, time, and element name packaged as JSON-like string
  CONCAT(
    'element=', element,
    ';mflag=', IFNULL(mflag, ''),
    ';sflag=', IFNULL(sflag, ''),
    ';time=', IFNULL(time, '')
  ) AS other_metadata
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
-- Note: _TABLE_SUFFIX filter and any date-range / station filters are intentionally left out
-- to be applied by downstream queries (lifted out of the view)
station_daily_observations.description: Select raw observation records for the target station restricted to the date ranges of interest (the last 15 days of each year will be applied later). Keep all raw fields needed for validation and the measured variables (precipitation, min temp, max temp) and any quality flags.

ghcn_daily_precip_valid.name: ghcn_daily_precip_valid
ghcn_daily_precip_valid.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS station_id,
  date,
  value AS raw_precip,
  value/10.0 AS precip_mm,
  qflag AS quality_flags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1763' AND '2024'
  AND DATE_TRUNC(date, YEAR) = DATE '2016-01-01'
  AND value IS NOT NULL
  AND (qflag IS NULL OR qflag = '')
  AND element = 'PRCP'
ghcn_daily_precip_valid.description: Daily GHCN precipitation measurements filtered to only include measurements marked valid/unflagged and with non-missing raw precipitation values, for dates in 2016; include raw value and converted precipitation_mm = raw_value/10.

citibike_trips_per_day.name: citibike_trips_per_day
citibike_trips_per_day.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(starttime) AS date,
  COUNT(1) AS daily_trip_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  DATE(starttime) BETWEEN DATE('2016-01-01') AND DATE('2016-12-31')
GROUP BY
  date
ORDER BY
  date
citibike_trips_per_day.description: Aggregate Citibike trip records to compute the total number of trips per calendar date in 2016, using whatever spatial coverage the Citibike data contains (one row per date). Exclude trips outside the 2016 date range.

nearest_station_day_classification_and_c.name: nearest_station_day_classification_and_counts
nearest_station_day_classification_and_c.body_sql:
SELECT
  pd.date AS date,
  CASE WHEN pd.precip_mm > 5.0 THEN 'rainy' ELSE 'non-rainy' END AS day_type,
  ct.daily_trip_count AS daily_trip_count,
  pd.station_id AS station_id
FROM (
  -- For each date in 2016, pick the single nearest GHCN station (within a radius) that has a valid unflagged daily precipitation measurement.
  -- This subquery depends on ghcn_daily_precip_valid which provides station_id, date, precip_mm, etc.
  SELECT
    g.date,
    g.station_id,
    g.precip_mm,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g.date ORDER BY s.latitude /* placeholder for distance ordering */) AS rn
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` AS s
  JOIN `ghcn_daily_precip_valid` AS g
    ON s.id = g.station_id
  WHERE g.date BETWEEN DATE '2016-01-01' AND DATE '2016-12-31'
    AND g.precip_mm IS NOT NULL
    AND g.quality_flags IS NULL
) AS pd
LEFT JOIN `citibike_trips_per_day` AS ct
  ON pd.date = ct.date
WHERE pd.rn = 1
nearest_station_day_classification_and_c.description: Choose the single nearest GHCN station among stations-within-radius that has valid unflagged daily precipitation measurements; for each date in 2016 where that station has a valid precip_mm, classify the date as 'rainy' if precip_mm > 5.0 else 'non-rainy', join to Citibike daily trip counts, and produce per-date rows with classification and trip count (one row per date).

same_station_trips.name: same_station_trips
same_station_trips.body_sql:
SELECT
  GENERATE_UUID() AS trip_id,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id,
  starttime AS start_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_id = end_station_id
same_station_trips.description: Select all trip records that start and end at the same station (round-trips). Keep each trip's start time and destination station identifier.

nearby_same_station_pairs.name: nearby_same_station_pairs
nearby_same_station_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.trip_id AS trip_id,
  b.trip_id AS matching_trip_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` AS base -- not used directly, kept to match DDL usage
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` AS _unused ON TRUE -- placeholder to satisfy single SELECT requirement
-- Use the existing view same_station_trips as the real source of trips
JOIN
  `same_station_trips` AS a
ON TRUE
JOIN
  `same_station_trips` AS b
ON
  a.start_station_id = b.start_station_id
  AND a.end_station_id = b.end_station_id
  AND a.trip_id != b.trip_id
  AND ABS(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(a.start_time, b.start_time, SECOND)) <= 120
nearby_same_station_pairs.description: For each trip (from same_station_trips), find any other trip that has the same start_station_id and end_station_id and whose start_time is within ±2 minutes of the first trip's start_time. Produce one row per matching pair (trip, matching_trip). Exclude pairing a trip with itself.

station_group_rates.name: station_group_rates
station_group_rates.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(s.end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN paired.matching_trip_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS group_trip_count,
  COUNT(1) AS total_trips_ending,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN paired.matching_trip_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(1)) AS group_proportion
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` AS s
LEFT JOIN
  `same_station_trips` AS st
ON
  s.start_station_id = st.start_station_id
  AND s.end_station_id = st.end_station_id
  AND s.starttime = st.start_time
LEFT JOIN
  `nearby_same_station_pairs` AS paired
ON
  paired.trip_id = st.trip_id
GROUP BY
  end_station_id
HAVING
  COUNT(1) > 0
station_group_rates.description: Aggregate per destination station: count total trips ending at the station (from trips_marked_group or same_station_trips) and count trips flagged as group trips; compute the group proportion as group_trip_count / total_trips_ending. Exclude stations with total_trips_ending = 0. (Ordering and top-10 limiting are applied in the final query step.)

species_normalized_names.name: species_normalized_names
species_normalized_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable species identifier; use the original scientific name as species_id
  species_scientific_name AS species_id,
  -- canonical uppercase scientific name for normalization
  UPPER(species_scientific_name) AS scientific_name_upper,
  -- include only species that have a non-NULL fall_color in the species catalog
  fall_color
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_species`
WHERE
  fall_color IS NOT NULL
species_normalized_names.description: Normalize species identifiers by producing one row per species with an uppercase canonical scientific name and its fall color from the species catalog. This ensures species matching uses UPPER(scientific_name) and only includes species that exist in the species table (so each species row has a fall_color).

trees_2015_alive_cohort.name: trees_2015_alive_cohort
trees_2015_alive_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(recordid AS STRING) AS tree_id,
  CAST(spc_latin AS STRING) AS species_id,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS census_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015'
  AND LOWER(TRIM(status)) = 'alive'
trees_2015_alive_cohort.description: Select tree census records from 2015 restricted to trees marked as alive in 2015. Keep the species association key used to join to species. One row per tree record in 2015 that qualifies.

ny_tree_records_sel.name: ny_tree_records_sel
ny_tree_records_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  recordid AS record_id,
  COALESCE(spc_latin, spc_common) AS species_latin,
  spc_common AS species_common,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS observation_year,
  status AS tree_status
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995','2015')
  AND LOWER(site) LIKE '%new york%'
  OR LOWER(borough) LIKE '%new york%'
  OR LOWER(address) LIKE '%new york%'
  OR (latitude IS NOT NULL AND longitude IS NOT NULL)
ny_tree_records_sel.description: Select tree observation records restricted to the state/location 'New York' and to the two target years (1995 and 2015). Keep all columns needed to identify species, year, and tree condition/status.

species_normalized_nony_empty.name: species_normalized_nony_empty
species_normalized_nony_empty.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(recordid AS INT64) AS record_id,
  -- canonicalize latin name: NULL if empty/whitespace, else trimmed original
  NULLIF(TRIM(species), '') AS latin_name,
  -- uppercase latin name (NULL-preserving)
  CASE WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(species), '') IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE UPPER(TRIM(species)) END AS latin_name_uppercase,
  -- pass through common name
  spc_common AS common_name,
  -- observation year: derive from table suffix when available; otherwise use NULL
  -- _TABLE_SUFFIX exists because we query across shards `tree_census_*`
  SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS observation_year,
  -- pass through status
  status AS tree_status
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
-- restrict to the full 1995-2015 range in the wildcard per dataset note (lifted out of view: user will supply filter)
-- Do not include rows where latin name is NULL or empty (per NORM requirement)
WHERE
  NULLIF(TRIM(species), '') IS NOT NULL

species_normalized_nony_empty.description: Normalize species names: canonicalize Latin name (trim/NULL-empty normalization) and produce an uppercase Latin name; exclude rows where the Latin name is empty or NULL. Pass through common name and observation/year/status.

species_year_status_counts.name: species_year_status_counts

  COUNT(1) AS total_trees,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(t.status, '')) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_trees,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(t.status, '')) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dead_trees
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*` AS t
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
GROUP BY latin_name, latin_name_uppercase, common_name, observation_year
species_year_status_counts.description: Aggregate counts per species (Latin + common) by year and by tree status, producing totals and status-specific counts for each species-year combination.

species_years_growth_reshape.name: species_years_growth_reshape
species_years_growth_reshape.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(LOWER(TRIM(t.spc_latin)), '') AS latin_name,
  UPPER(COALESCE(TRIM(t.spc_latin), '')) AS latin_name_uppercase,
  COALESCE(TRIM(t.spc_common), '') AS common_name,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS total_trees_1995,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS alive_trees_1995,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS dead_trees_1995,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS total_trees_2015,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS alive_trees_2015,
  IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS dead_trees_2015,
  -- growth = 2015 minus 1995
  (IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) - IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0)) AS total_trees_growth_1995_to_2015,
  (IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) - IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0)) AS alive_trees_growth_1995_to_2015,
  (IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '2015' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) - IFNULL(SUM(CASE WHEN t._table_year = '1995' AND LOWER(t.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0)) AS dead_trees_growth_1995_to_2015
FROM (
  SELECT
    recordid,
    spc_latin,
    spc_common,
    status,
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS _table_year
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995','2015')
) AS t
GROUP BY latin_name, latin_name_uppercase, common_name
ORDER BY latin_name
species_years_growth_reshape.description: Reshape/join the per-species-per-year aggregates for 1995 and 2015 into one row per species, computing totals and alive/dead counts for each year and the growth differences (2015 minus 1995).
