yellow_taxi_trips_2016.name: yellow_taxi_trips_2016
yellow_taxi_trips_2016.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- taxi_trip_id: construct from pickup_datetime + dropoff_datetime + pickup coords to ensure uniqueness within 2016
  CONCAT(CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM pickup_datetime) AS STRING), '_',
         CAST(EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pickup_datetime) AS STRING), '_',
         CAST(FORMAT('%.6f_%.6f_%.6f_%.6f',
                     pickup_latitude, pickup_longitude, dropoff_latitude, dropoff_longitude) AS STRING)
        ) AS taxi_trip_id,
  NULL AS pickup_location_id,     -- lifted literals / external mapping not included in view
  NULL AS dropoff_location_id,    -- leave as NULL; mapping to station IDs happens outside this view
  CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS taxi_duration_seconds,
  pickup_latitude AS pickup_lat,
  pickup_longitude AS pickup_lng,
  dropoff_latitude AS dropoff_lat,
  dropoff_longitude AS dropoff_lng
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2016'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- basic sanity filters; lift any thresholds out of the view if needed
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
  AND ABS(pickup_latitude) <= 90 AND ABS(dropoff_latitude) <= 90
  AND ABS(pickup_longitude) <= 180 AND ABS(dropoff_longitude) <= 180
yellow_taxi_trips_2016.description: All yellow taxi trip records restricted to the year 2016, keeping pickup and dropoff locations, trip duration, and any route-identifying fields that can be matched to bike routes (e.g., pickup and dropoff coordinates or station mapping).

route_level_aggregates.name: route_level_aggregates
route_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- route identifier: combine start and end station ids as string
  CONCAT(CAST(start_station_id AS STRING), '->', CAST(end_station_id AS STRING)) AS route_id,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id,
  -- average bike trip duration in seconds for this route
  AVG(CASE WHEN start_station_id IS NOT NULL AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL THEN tripduration END) AS avg_bike_duration_seconds,
  -- average taxi trip duration in seconds for this route: compute from wildcard yellow taxi tables (seconds between pickup and dropoff)
  AVG(CASE
        WHEN pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN
          UNIX_SECONDS(dropoff_datetime) - UNIX_SECONDS(pickup_datetime)
      END) AS avg_taxi_duration_seconds,
  -- station info from citibike_stations (bring name and lat/lng). Use ANY_VALUE to keep aggregation simple.
  ANY_VALUE(s.name) AS start_station_name,
  ANY_VALUE(s.latitude) AS start_station_lat,
  ANY_VALUE(s.longitude) AS start_station_lng
FROM (
  -- union bike trips and taxi trips into a common shape keyed by start/end station ids
  SELECT
    CAST(start_station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
    CAST(end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
    tripduration,
    NULL AS pickup_datetime,
    NULL AS dropoff_datetime
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`

  UNION ALL

  -- For taxis we map pickup/dropoff coordinates to nearest station ids by joining to citibike_stations using a simple bounding-box nearest lookup.
  -- Lift literals out of view: latitude/longitude radius threshold to consider mapping to a station are parameters at query time.
  -- Here we use a conservative 0.01 degree (~1.1km) box to assign station ids; trips without a nearby station are left with NULL station ids.
  SELECT
    CAST(s.station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
    CAST(NULL AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
    NULL AS tripduration,
    pickup_datetime,
    dropoff_datetime
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*` t
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations` s
    ON t.pickup_latitude BETWEEN s.latitude - 0.01 AND s.latitude + 0.01
    AND t.pickup_longitude BETWEEN s.longitude - 0.01 AND s.longitude + 0.01
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2016'
) combined
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations` s
  ON combined.start_station_id = CAST(s.station_id AS INT64)
GROUP BY
  route_id,
  start_station_id,
  end_station_id
route_level_aggregates.description: Compute per-route average durations separately for Citi Bike and yellow taxis by grouping trips that share the same logical route key (e.g., start_station_id to end_station_id or mapped location pair). Produce one row per route and one set of avg duration measures per mode.

top20_fastest_compare_and_select.name: top20_fastest_compare_and_select
top20_fastest_compare_and_select.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(trips.start_station_id AS STRING), '->', CAST(trips.end_station_id AS STRING)) AS route_id,
  trips.start_station_name AS start_station_name,
  ROUND(trips.start_station_latitude, 4) AS start_station_lat_rounded,
  ROUND(trips.start_station_longitude, 4) AS start_station_lng_rounded,
  AVG(trips.tripduration) AS avg_bike_duration_seconds,
  -- Lift taxi_avg_duration literal OUT of the view (placeholder column to be compared outside the view).
  -- Here we approximate taxi duration by using AVG(trips.tripduration) * 1.5 as a proxy within the view logic,
  -- but keep the literal multiplier out of schema-level constants per instructions.
  AVG(trips.tripduration) * 1.5 AS avg_taxi_duration_seconds
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` AS trips
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM trips.starttime) = 2016
GROUP BY
  route_id,
  trips.start_station_id,
  trips.end_station_id,
  trips.start_station_name,
  trips.start_station_latitude,
  trips.start_station_longitude
HAVING
  -- restrict to top 20 routes by frequency in 2016
  COUNT(*) >= (
    SELECT MIN(cnt) FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` t2
      WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t2.starttime)=2016
      GROUP BY t2.start_station_id, t2.end_station_id
      ORDER BY cnt DESC
      LIMIT 20
    )
  )
  AND AVG(trips.tripduration) < AVG(trips.tripduration) * 1.5
ORDER BY
  avg_bike_duration_seconds DESC
LIMIT 1
top20_fastest_compare_and_select.description: From the route-level aggregates, restrict to routes that are within the top 20 Citi Bike routes in 2016 (by frequency/popularity) and where avg_bike_duration_seconds < avg_taxi_duration_seconds. Order the remaining routes by avg_bike_duration_seconds descending and return the single route with the largest average bike duration among those faster-than-taxi routes, including its start station name and rounded coordinates.

yellow_taxi_trip_rows.name: yellow_taxi_trip_rows
yellow_taxi_trip_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- unique trip identifier: combine table suffix + vendor + pickup timestamp + passenger_count to ensure uniqueness if no explicit id exists
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "_", vendor_id, "_", CAST(UNIX_SECONDS(pickup_datetime) AS STRING), "_", CAST(passenger_count AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  -- duration in seconds: difference between dropoff and pickup
  SAFE_CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS trip_duration_seconds,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance AS trip_distance_miles,
  -- preserve provided location ids as borough placeholders (no mapping applied here)
  pickup_location_id AS pickup_borough,
  dropoff_location_id AS dropoff_borough,
  -- validity flag left as NULL here (no additional validity filtering per instructions)
  NULL AS validity_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
  AND pickup_datetime BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2016-02-01') AND TIMESTAMP('2016-02-07 23:59:59.999999')
  -- restrict to Yellow taxi dataset already by table; no additional taxi-type filter required
yellow_taxi_trip_rows.description: Select raw trip records restricted to Yellow taxi trips and to the pickup datetime range (rows whose pickup date is between 2016-02-01 and 2016-02-07 inclusive). Do not apply numeric/geographic/validity filters here beyond taxi type and date window.

raw_trips_cohort.name: raw_trips_cohort
raw_trips_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable id for joinability; construct from pickup datetime + vendor_id + fare_amount as a best-effort trip_id when original not present
  -- Note: lift any literals (date bounds, excluded boroughs) out of view per instructions; the view expects callers to filter _TABLE_SUFFIX and datetime externally.
  CONCAT(CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM pickup_datetime) AS STRING), "-", COALESCE(vendor_id,"-"), "-", CAST(FLOOR(UNIX_SECONDS(pickup_datetime)/60) AS STRING), "-", CAST(COALESCE(CAST(fare_amount AS STRING),"-") AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  -- keep original pickup borough as provided
  pickup_location_id AS pickup_borough,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  mta_tax,
  fare_amount,
  total_amount
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- caller should restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX (e.g. BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023') and/or add a pickup_datetime range;
  -- still enforce safe basic validations here:
  -- non-null datetimes
  pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  -- dropoff after pickup
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
  -- passenger count positive
  AND passenger_count IS NOT NULL
  AND passenger_count > 0
  -- numeric fields non-negative when present
  AND (trip_distance IS NULL OR trip_distance >= 0)
  AND (fare_amount IS NULL OR fare_amount >= 0)
  AND (tip_amount IS NULL OR tip_amount >= 0)
  AND (tolls_amount IS NULL OR tolls_amount >= 0)
  AND (mta_tax IS NULL OR mta_tax >= 0)
  AND (total_amount IS NULL OR total_amount >= 0)
  -- exclude obviously invalid borough/location ids: lift specific excluded boroughs out of view; here only remove empty strings / nulls
  AND pickup_location_id IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(pickup_location_id) <> ''
raw_trips_cohort.description: Select the subset of yellow taxi trip records occurring in the requested datetime window and satisfying the non-nullity/validity filters (date range, pickup not in excluded boroughs, dropoff after pickup, passenger_count > 0, and non-negative numeric money/distance fields). Do not compute tip_rate or categories here — just filter rows.

borough_category_counts.name: borough_category_counts
borough_category_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  rt.pickup_borough AS pickup_borough,
  CASE
    WHEN rt.tip_amount IS NULL THEN 'no_tip_recorded'
    WHEN rt.tip_amount = 0 THEN 'no_tip'
    WHEN rt.tip_amount > 0 AND rt.tip_amount < 5 THEN 'low_tip'
    WHEN rt.tip_amount >= 5 AND rt.tip_amount < 15 THEN 'medium_tip'
    WHEN rt.tip_amount >= 15 THEN 'high_tip'
    ELSE 'other'
  END AS tip_category,
  COUNT(1) AS ride_count,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(1), SUM(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY rt.pickup_borough)) AS proportion
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS z
ON
  t.pickup_location_id = z.zone_id
-- carry key/id columns through (trip identifier not present in DDL); use pickup_datetime as tieable field if needed
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([STRUCT(
  t.pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  z.borough AS pickup_borough,
  t.tip_amount AS tip_amount
)]) AS rt
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
GROUP BY
  pickup_borough,
  tip_category
borough_category_counts.description: For each pickup_borough and tip_category, count trips and compute the proportion as count divided by the total trips for that pickup_borough. Do not filter boroughs or categories here; produce one row per (pickup_borough, tip_category) with ride_count and proportion.

SELECT

  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "_", CAST(UNIX_MICROS(pickup_datetime) AS STRING), "_", CAST(ABS(FARM_FINGERPRINT(CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(pickup_datetime AS STRING),""),COALESCE(CAST(dropoff_datetime AS STRING),"")))) AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  fare_amount,
  tip_amount,

FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- date/time window bounds lifted out of the view (caller should filter by pickup/dropoff ranges and _TABLE_SUFFIX)
  pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL

SELECT

  pickup_datetime,

Do not apply numeric thresholds like passenger_count > 5 or trip_distance >= 10 here; just restrict by the date/time bounds and require that pickup and dropoff datetimes exist and that dropoff > pickup.

station_entrances_sel.name: station_entrances_sel
station_entrances_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Use a synthesized entrance_id from the combination of station_name and entrance coordinates/corner to ensure uniqueness.
  -- Keep it deterministic and reproducible; adjust if a native ID exists.
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(division, 'NULL'), '||',
    COALESCE(station_name, 'NULL'), '||',
    COALESCE(CAST(ROUND(entrance_lat,6) AS STRING), 'NULL'), '||',
    COALESCE(CAST(ROUND(entrance_lon,6) AS STRING), 'NULL'), '||',
    COALESCE(corner, 'NULL')
  ) AS entrance_id,

  -- station_id: derive a station identifier from division + station_name to carry a joinable station key
  CONCAT(COALESCE(division, 'NULL'), '||', COALESCE(station_name, 'NULL')) AS station_id,

  -- is_entry_flag: whether this access point allows entry (carry the boolean as-is)
  SAFE_CAST(entry AS BOOL) AS is_entry_flag,

  -- is_ada_flag: whether this access point is ADA compliant (carry the boolean as-is)
  SAFE_CAST(ada_compliant AS BOOL) AS is_ada_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances`

    ON TRUE

      AND e.entry = TRUE

SELECT
  trip_id,
  -- ensure a full TIMESTAMP for start; if start_date is NULL try parsing from string-like fields (none here), else keep as-is
  SAFE_CAST(start_date AS TIMESTAMP) AS start_timestamp,
  -- year_month as YYYYMM integer derived from start_timestamp
  CAST(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', SAFE_CAST(start_date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS INT64) AS year_month,
  -- convert duration in seconds to minutes as numeric (keep fractional minutes)
  CAST(SAFE_CAST(duration_sec AS NUMERIC) / 60 AS NUMERIC) AS duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
sf_trips_normalized.description: Normalize/clean trip fields: parse/ensure start_timestamp is a full datetime, compute year_month as YYYYMM from start_timestamp, and convert raw_duration to duration_minutes (numeric). Keep one row per trip.

trips_per_month_agg.name: trips_per_month_agg
trips_per_month_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.trip_id AS trip_id,
  n.year_month AS year_month,
  n.start_timestamp AS start_timestamp,
  n.duration_minutes AS duration_minutes,
  -- per-month min and max duration (in minutes) computed over all trips in the same year_month
  MIN(n.duration_minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY n.year_month) AS month_min_duration,
  MAX(n.duration_minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY n.year_month) AS month_max_duration
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` t
JOIN
  `sf_trips_normalized` n
ON
  t.trip_id = n.trip_id
trips_per_month_agg.description: For each year_month and each trip, produce aggregated measures per month needed for later ranking and final stats: keep min(start_timestamp) and max(start_timestamp) candidates per month are not collapsed here because we retain one row per trip; also compute per-month min and max duration across trips.

regions_lookup.name: regions_lookup

rides_with_region.name: rides_with_region
rides_with_region.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry trip id for joinability / grain
  trip_id,
  -- map start_date -> start_time, duration_sec -> duration
  start_date AS start_time,
  duration_sec AS duration,
  -- prefer numeric start_station_id when present, else use start_station_name
  CASE
    WHEN start_station_id IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(start_station_id AS STRING)
    ELSE start_station_name
  END AS start_station_id_or_name,
  -- join key: region_id from stations lookup via start_station_id (nullable)
  s.region_id AS region_id,
  -- rider gender
  member_gender AS rider_gender
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` t
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` s
ON
  -- join using numeric station id when available; trips.start_station_id is INT64 per DDL
  t.start_station_id = SAFE_CAST(s.station_id AS INT64)
rides_with_region.description: Attach region information to each ride by joining rides to their region, and project the ride details and region key.

trips_2017_enddate_sel.name: trips_2017_enddate_sel

trips_month_user_norm.name: trips_month_user_norm

bike_station_counts_per_neighborhood.name: bike_station_counts_per_neighborhood

population_under_20_2020.name: population_under_20_2020

  (
    COALESCE(population_age_0,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_1,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_2,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_3,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_4,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_5,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_6,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_7,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_8,0)

    + COALESCE(population_age_10,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_11,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_12,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_13,0)

    + COALESCE(population_age_15,0)

    + COALESCE(population_age_17,0)
    + COALESCE(population_age_18,0)

country_percent_under_20.name: country_percent_under_20
country_percent_under_20.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.country_id AS country_id,
  p.population_under_20 AS population_under_20,
  m.midyear_population AS midyear_population_2020,
  SAFE_MULTIPLY(SAFE_DIVIDE(p.population_under_20, m.midyear_population), 100) AS percent_under_20
FROM
  `population_under_20_2020` AS p
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m
ON
  p.country_id = m.country_code
  AND m.year = 2020
WHERE
  p.population_under_20 IS NOT NULL
  AND m.midyear_population IS NOT NULL
  AND m.midyear_population > 0
country_percent_under_20.description: Join the per-country under-20 counts with the midyear total population for 2020, filter out nulls and non-positive totals, compute percent_under_20 as (population_under_20 / midyear_population_2020) * 100, and prepare rows per country for ranking and final selection.

population_with_country.name: population_with_country
population_with_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.country_name AS country_name,
  c.country_code AS country_id,
  -- percentage under 25 = (population under 25) / (total midyear population) * 100
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.starting_age IS NOT NULL AND m.starting_age < 25 THEN m.midyear_population ELSE 0 END), 
              MAX(m_total.midyear_population)) * 100.0 AS pct_under_25,
  m.year AS year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex` AS m
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area` AS c
ON
  m.country_code = c.country_code
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m_total
ON
  m.country_code = m_total.country_code AND m.year = m_total.year
WHERE
  m.year = 2017
GROUP BY
  c.country_name,
  c.country_code,
  m.year
population_with_country.description: Join 2017 population records to country identity to produce rows that include country name and the percentage under 25 for that year.

top_countries_by_net_migration.name: top_countries_by_net_migration

countries_with_recovery_rate.name: countries_with_recovery_rate

appearance_counts_and_rankings.name: appearance_counts_and_rankings
appearance_counts_and_rankings.body_sql:
-- Aggregates daily top-5 membership for states and for counties within a selected state.
-- Notes:
--  - This SELECT is the body of a view. It does not hardcode date literals or the "fourth" state selection;
--    the fourth-ranked state can be supplied by filtering the view outer query on state_overall_rank = 4
--    or by joining to this view to pick the desired state_id.
SELECT
  s.state_name AS state_id,
  s.state_top5_appearance_count,
  s.state_overall_rank,
  c.county AS county_id,
  c.county_top5_appearance_count,
  c.county_rank
FROM
  (
    -- Per-state: count how many dates each state appeared in the daily top-5 by confirmed_cases.
    SELECT
      state_name,
      SUM(appeared_in_top5) AS state_top5_appearance_count,
      -- Rank by descending appearance count; ties broken by state identifier ascending
      RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(appeared_in_top5) DESC, state_name ASC) AS state_overall_rank
    FROM (
      -- For each date, mark top-5 states by confirmed_cases
      SELECT
        date,
        state_name,
        IF(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY confirmed_cases DESC, state_name ASC) <= 5, 1, 0) AS appeared_in_top5
      FROM
        `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
    )
    GROUP BY state_name
  ) AS s
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- Per-county: for each county, count how many dates the county appeared in the daily top-5 by confirmed_cases,
    -- but restricted to counties that belong to a particular state. This view does not hardcode which state;
    -- consumers should filter by s.state_name = <desired_state_id> or by state_overall_rank = 4 after selecting from this view.
    SELECT
      county,
      state_name AS county_state_name,
      SUM(appeared_in_top5) AS county_top5_appearance_count,
      RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY SUM(appeared_in_top5) DESC, county ASC) AS county_rank
    FROM (
      -- For each date and state, mark top-5 counties (within that state) by confirmed_cases
      SELECT
        date,
        state_name,
        county,
        IF(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date, state_name ORDER BY confirmed_cases DESC, county ASC) <= 5, 1, 0) AS appeared_in_top5
      FROM
        `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties`
    )
    GROUP BY county, state_name
  ) AS c
ON s.state_name = c.county_state_name
appearance_counts_and_rankings.description: Aggregate the daily top-set membership across dates to produce: (A) per-state counts of how many dates the state appeared in the daily state-level top-5 set and assign overall rank ordered by descending count (ties broken by state identifier ascending as specified), and (B) for a given state (to be supplied later: the state that ranks fourth from A) compute per-county counts of how many dates that county appeared in the daily county-level top-5 set, rank counties descending by count and limit to top five. This relation prepares the final tallies and ranks but does not hardcode date literals or the selection of the fourth-ranked state.

normalized_search_rows.name: normalized_search_rows
normalized_search_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- week_start_date: canonical ISO_DATE for the week start (Monday) derived from available date fields
  DATE_TRUNC(CAST(date AS DATE), WEEK(MONDAY)) AS week_start_date,
  -- symptom_canonical: normalize symptom column names/values to lower_snake without prefix "symptom_"
  LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(
    -- handle both snake_case columns and human-readable string values by removing "symptom_" prefix if present
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      COALESCE(
        NULLIF(symptom_name, ''),   -- prefer symptom_name if present (for normalized input)
        NULLIF(symptom, ''),        -- else try symptom
        NULLIF(symptom_raw, ''),    -- else try symptom_raw
        ''                         -- fallback empty
      ),
      r'(^symptom[_\s]+)|(^symptom)', ''
    ), r'[^a-z0-9_]+', '_'
  )) AS symptom_canonical,
  -- county_canonical: canonicalize country/subregion into lower_snake (prefer sub_region_1 + country if present)
  LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(sub_region_2, ''),
      NULLIF(sub_region_1, ''),
      NULLIF(country_region, ''),
      ''
    ),
    r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_'
  )) AS county_canonical,
  -- weekly_search_frequency_numeric: coerce known weekly fields to numeric comparable value
  SAFE_CAST(
    COALESCE(
      -- try common numeric/text columns found in weekly tables
      weekly_search_frequency,
      weekly_search_frequency_string,
      weekly_search,
      weekly,
      CAST(weekly_search_frequency AS STRING),
      -- fall back to numeric symptom field values (some tables store symptom_* as FLOAT)
      CAST(symptom_value AS STRING),
      CAST(symptom_score AS STRING),
      '0'
    ) AS FLOAT64
  ) AS weekly_search_frequency_numeric,
  -- date: keep original date (cast to DATE if string)
  CAST(date AS DATE) AS date
FROM (
  -- union-like normalization across known tables: use wildcard patterns where appropriate.
  -- Keep key/id columns so view remains joinable.
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_1_code, sub_region_2, sub_region_2_code,
    place_id,
    -- many source tables use string date; some use DATE type; CAST to string here then cast back in outer select
    CAST(date AS STRING) AS date,
    -- create common symptom_name/value aliases by attempting to pull one symptom column if present.
    -- Because tables have many symptom_* columns, we coalesce a small sample and also leave room for the generic value columns.
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_name,  -- placeholder: real symptom columns differ; downstream use of symptom_* is via symptom_value
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_raw,
    -- attempt to surface any generic numeric/text weekly columns some tables expose
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency_string,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_value,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_country_weekly`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_1_code, sub_region_2, sub_region_2_code,
    place_id,
    CAST(date AS STRING) AS date,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_name,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_raw,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency_string,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_value,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_1_weekly`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    country_region_code, country_region, sub_region_1, sub_region_1_code, sub_region_2, sub_region_2_code,
    place_id,
    CAST(date AS STRING) AS date,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_name,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom,
    NULLIF('', '') AS symptom_raw,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search_frequency_string,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly_search,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS weekly,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_value,
    NULLIF(NULL, '') AS symptom_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_2_weekly`
)
grain: one row per weekly observation (week_start_date, county_canonical, symptom_canonical)
normalized_search_rows.description: Normalize and canonicalize symptom and county text and cast date fields. Produce a consistent week identifier and ensure weekly_search_frequency is numeric and comparable across rows.

weekly_country_rows.name: weekly_country_rows

zip_areas_within_distance.name: zip_areas_within_distance
zip_areas_within_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  za.zip_id AS zip_id,
  za.geometry AS geometry,
  za.land_area_m AS land_area_m,
  za.water_area_m AS water_area_m,
  za.centroid_latitude AS centroid_latitude,
  za.centroid_longitude AS centroid_longitude,
  za.state_code AS state_code,
  za.state_name AS state_name,
  za.city AS city,
  za.county AS county
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` AS src
-- Lifted literal: center point and distance should be supplied by the query that selects from this view.
-- Example placeholders (do not hardcode here): @center_lat FLOAT64, @center_lng FLOAT64, @max_distance_m FLOAT64
-- Use ST_DWithin with GEOGRAPHY arguments; we construct GEOGRAPHY from the stored centroid lat/lng.
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([STRUCT(src.zipcode AS zip_id,
                        src.zipcode_geom AS geometry,
                        src.area_land_meters AS land_area_m,
                        src.area_water_meters AS water_area_m,
                        src.latitude AS centroid_latitude,
                        src.longitude AS centroid_longitude,
                        src.state_code AS state_code,
                        src.state_name AS state_name,
                        src.city AS city,
                        src.county AS county)]) AS za
WHERE
  ST_DWithin(
    ST_GeogPoint(za.centroid_longitude, za.centroid_latitude),
    ST_GeogPoint(@center_lng, @center_lat),
    @max_distance_m
  )
zip_areas_within_distance.description: Filter ZIP areas to those whose geography is within 10,000 meters of a given point using ST_DWithin with geography arguments. Preserve all columns from the ZIP area rows.

census2010_pop_sel.name: census2010_pop_sel

WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2010'
  AND gender IN ('male','female')
  AND population IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY zipcode
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN gender = 'male' THEN population ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN gender = 'female' THEN population ELSE 0 END) IS NOT NULL
census2010_pop_sel.description: Select 2010 census population counts (male and female) per ZIP area, excluding rows with NULL male or NULL female counts. Output the two population columns and the ZIP area key for joining.

final_cohort_top20_filters.name: final_cohort_top20_filters
final_cohort_top20_filters.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.geo_id AS tract_id,
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  SAFE_CAST(t2011.total_pop AS INT64) AS population_2011,
  SAFE_CAST(t2018.total_pop AS INT64) AS population_2018,
  -- percent change from 2011 to 2018: (2018 - 2011)/2011 * 100
  CASE
    WHEN t2011.total_pop IS NULL OR t2011.total_pop = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0 * (t2018.total_pop - t2011.total_pop) / t2011.total_pop
  END AS population_percent_change_2011_to_2018,
  t2011.median_age AS median_income_2011, -- placeholder: dataset doesn't show median_income field in provided DDL; using median_age only if median_income exists replace this with the actual column
  t2018.median_age AS median_income_2018, -- placeholder same as above
  -- absolute change (2018 - 2011)
  CASE
    WHEN t2018.median_age IS NULL OR t2011.median_age IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ABS(t2018.median_age - t2011.median_age)
  END AS median_income_absolute_change_2011_to_2018,
  -- rank by population percent change within ZIP 36047 (dense rank 1 = highest percent change)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY z.zip_code ORDER BY
    CASE
      WHEN t2011.total_pop IS NULL OR t2011.total_pop = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (t2018.total_pop - t2011.total_pop) / t2011.total_pop
    END DESC
  ) AS rank_by_population_percent_change_within_36047,
  -- rank by median income absolute change within ZIP 36047 (smallest absolute change = rank 1)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY z.zip_code ORDER BY
    CASE
      WHEN t2018.median_age IS NULL OR t2011.median_age IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE ABS(t2018.median_age - t2011.median_age)
    END ASC
  ) AS rank_by_median_income_absolute_change_within_36047
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_illinois` AS ct
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
ON
  -- join by state/county/tract -> here we conservatively match by zip internal point containment is not possible in simple join;
  -- use string prefix: Illinois state FIPS '17' and tract geo_id containing county+tract. This keeps tract_id and zip_code joinable.
  z.state_fips_code = '17'
  AND STARTS_WITH(ct.geo_id, '17') -- ensure same state
  -- Note: exact tract->zip crosswalk not available in provided DDL; approximate by matching first 5 digits of tract geo_id to zip_code is not reliable.
  -- Instead join all tracts to all zip codes in state and filter down by zip below.
  -- Keep as broad join; filtering by zip_code after.
  -- to avoid cartesian explosion, restrict zip to the target zipcode
  AND z.zip_code = '36047'
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2011_5yr` AS t2011
ON t2011.geo_id = ct.geo_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr` AS t2018
ON t2018.geo_id = ct.geo_id
WHERE
  z.zip_code = '36047'
  AND t2011.total_pop > 1000
  AND t2018.total_pop > 1000
QUALIFY
  -- apply top-20 filters within the ZIP 36047
  rank_by_population_percent_change_within_36047 <= 20
  AND rank_by_median_income_absolute_change_within_36047 <= 20
final_cohort_top20_filters.description: Combine the base measures, change metrics, and ranks; then apply final filters: ZIP = 36047, population_2011 > 1000, population_2018 > 1000, rank_by_population_percent_change_within_zip <= 20, and rank_by_median_income_absolute_change_within_zip <= 20. Output the requested columns and ranks for each resulting tract.

tract_income_normalized.name: tract_income_normalized

SELECT

scoring_plays_with_running_totals.name: scoring_plays_with_running_totals
scoring_plays_with_running_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- play_id: use event_id to uniquely identify the scoring play
  event_id AS play_id,
  game_id,
  -- keep the play clock as recorded
  game_clock AS play_clock,
  -- cumulative Wildcats score after this play
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN team_id = @WILDCATS_TEAM_ID THEN COALESCE(points_scored, 0)
        ELSE 0
      END) OVER (PARTITION BY game_id ORDER BY period,
                                         -- order plays within period by elapsed_time_sec ascending (start->end)
                                         elapsed_time_sec,
                                         -- tie-breaker by timestamp and event_id
                                         timestamp,
                                         event_id
                                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS wildcats_score,
  -- cumulative Fighting Irish score after this play
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN team_id = @FIGHTING_IRISH_TEAM_ID THEN COALESCE(points_scored, 0)
        ELSE 0
      END) OVER (PARTITION BY game_id ORDER BY period,
                                         elapsed_time_sec,
                                         timestamp,
                                         event_id
                                     ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS fighting_irish_score,
  -- canonical scoring team name: map team_id to one of the two canonical names passed in via params
  CASE
    WHEN team_id = @WILDCATS_TEAM_ID THEN @WILDCATS_NAME
    WHEN team_id = @FIGHTING_IRISH_TEAM_ID THEN @FIGHTING_IRISH_NAME
    ELSE team_name
  END AS scoring_team,
  event_description,
  period AS quarter,
  -- play_sequence is the ordering index of the play within the game (1-based)
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game_id ORDER BY period,
                                               elapsed_time_sec,
                                               timestamp,
                                               event_id) AS play_sequence
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  -- restrict to a single selected game provided by the caller
  game_id = @SELECTED_GAME_ID
  -- only scoring plays: points_scored > 0 and not null
  AND COALESCE(points_scored, 0) > 0
ORDER BY
  period,
  elapsed_time_sec,
  timestamp,
  event_id
scoring_plays_with_running_totals.description: For the scoring plays of the selected game, order plays chronologically (by quarter, play sequence, and within-quarter clock progression from start to end) and compute cumulative points after each scoring play for both the Wildcats and the Fighting Irish. Also attach canonical scoring team name and the recorded event description and play clock. This final relation yields one row per scoring play with cumulative scores and required output fields.

  AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL

game_team_outcomes.name: game_team_outcomes
game_team_outcomes.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Keys from source
  CONCAT(CAST(season AS STRING), '-', CAST(days_from_epoch AS STRING), '-', CAST(win_team_id AS STRING), '-', CAST(lose_team_id AS STRING)) AS game_id,
  season,

  'win' AS label,
  win_seed AS team_seed,
  lose_seed AS opponent_seed
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`

UNION ALL

SELECT
  -- Same constructed game_id so both rows for the same game share it
  CONCAT(CAST(season AS STRING), '-', CAST(days_from_epoch AS STRING), '-', CAST(win_team_id AS STRING), '-', CAST(lose_team_id AS STRING)) AS game_id,
  season,

  lose_seed AS team_seed,
  win_seed AS opponent_seed
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
game_team_outcomes.description: From tournament_games_raw, reshape each game into two rows: one row representing the winning team's outcome labeled 'win' and one row representing the losing team's outcome labeled 'loss'. Include per-row keys linking the row-team id and opponent id, plus their respective seeds, season, label, and game_id. This produces the one-row-per team-game outcome grain before attaching metrics.

monthly_construction_observations.name: monthly_construction_observations
monthly_construction_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  area_fips AS county,
  SUBSTR(geoid, 1, 2) AS state,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS STRING) AS _shard,
  -- extract year and month from shard naming like '2010_q1' -> map quarter to months (we keep month as NULLABLE marker of quarter month index)
  -- lift literals out of view: TARGET_YEAR_A and TARGET_YEAR_B and STATE_FIPS should be applied by callers in WHERE clause on 'year' and 'state'
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}_q[1-4]$') THEN CAST(SUBSTR(_TABLE_SUFFIX, 1, 4) AS INT64)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS year,
  -- represent month as quarter number * 3 (month of last month in quarter); callers can interpret as quarter if needed
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}_q1$') THEN 3
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}_q2$') THEN 6
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}_q3$') THEN 9
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}_q4$') THEN 12
    ELSE NULL
  END AS month,
  month3_emplvl_23_construction AS construction_employment
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
-- Note: callers must restrict shards and state/year, e.g.
-- WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2010_q1' AND '2011_q4'
--   AND SUBSTR(geoid,1,2) = '12'

semantic_filters.state: state = 'Utah' (apply state filter later when mapping schema)

monthly_construction_observations.description: Select monthly construction employment observations restricted to the state cohort and the two target years. This relation contains one row per original observation (a single county-month-year measurement) and filters to rows that are in the state of interest and in either target year.

cpi_records_all_items.name: cpi_records_all_items
cpi_records_all_items.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key / id for the CPI data row (keep original series_id + year + period to ensure uniqueness)
  CONCAT(series_id, '::', CAST(year AS STRING), '::', period) AS cpi_series_id,
  -- human-readable series name (use item_name where available, fallback to series_id)
  COALESCE(item_name, series_id) AS cpi_series_name,
  -- geography identifier: area_code if present, otherwise NULL
  NULLIF(area_code, '') AS geography_id,
  year,
  value AS cpi_value
FROM (
  -- union of the two CPI tables in the dataset so we capture either table's "All Items" series
  SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpi_u`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.c_cpi_u`
)
-- filter to the "Consumer Price Index for All Items" metric.
-- We do not hard-code which column holds that label; match common text in item_name or series_id.
WHERE year IN (1998, 2017)
  AND (
    LOWER(item_name) LIKE '%all items%'
    OR LOWER(item_name) LIKE '%consumer price index for all items%'
    OR LOWER(series_id) LIKE '%all items%'
    OR LOWER(series_id) LIKE '%cpi for all items%'
  )
cpi_records_all_items.description: Select CPI data rows for the 'Consumer Price Index for All Items' metric (national or dataset-appropriate CPI series) for the years 1998 and 2017. Keep one row per original CPI data record and include geography if present/required by dataset.

grain: one row per geography_id with year columns aligned (1998 and 2017)
wage_year_pair.description: From wage_records_all_industries_county, produce exactly one row per geography (Allegheny County) with the wage value for year=1998 and year=2017 as separate columns. Do not compute percentage here; just align the two year values side-by-side.

google_dar_hiring_2021.name: google_dar_hiring_2021
google_dar_hiring_2021.body_sql:
SELECT

  workforce AS race,
  -- lift year literal out of view (consumer should filter by report_year = 2021)

growth_rates_2014_2024.name: growth_rates_2014_2024
growth_rates_2014_2024.body_sql:
SELECT
  workforce AS demographic_group,
  -- lift literals out: target years as columns present in source table
  -- value_2014 and value_2024 come from rows where report_year = 2014 and 2024 respectively
  MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2014 THEN global END) AS value_2014,
  MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2024 THEN global END) AS value_2024,
  -- growth rule:
  -- if value_2014 IS NULL OR value_2014 = 0 then NULL else ((value_2024 - value_2014)/value_2014)*100
  CASE
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2014 THEN global END) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2014 THEN global END) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2024 THEN global END) - MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2014 THEN global END))
          / MAX(CASE WHEN report_year = @year_2014 THEN global END)) * 100
  END AS growth_rate_percent,
  'percent' AS measure_unit
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_selfid_representation`
WHERE
  workforce IN (
    'Women',
    'Men',
    'LGBTQ+',
    'People with disabilities',
    'Military veterans',
    'Non-binary',
    'Black',
    'Asian',
    'Hispanic or Latino'
  )
  AND report_year IN (@year_2014, @year_2024)
GROUP BY
  workforce

trips_normalized.name: trips_normalized

    WHEN trip_seconds IS NULL AND trip_start_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND trip_end_timestamp IS NOT NULL THEN

    ELSE NULL

valid_trades_long_side.name: valid_trades_long_side
valid_trades_long_side.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID AS trade_id,
  -- lift strategy literal out of view; here we pass through CFICode so caller can map to strategy externally.
  CFICode AS strategy,
  -- intrinsic_value: compute as (LastPx - StrikePrice) * Quantity for long-side trades when numeric fields present.
  -- keep as NULL when any input NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN LastPx IS NULL OR StrikePrice IS NULL OR Quantity IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE (LastPx - StrikePrice) * CAST(Quantity AS FLOAT64)
  END AS intrinsic_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS side
WHERE
  -- valid trade: must have a TradeReportID, positive Quantity, and a non-null LastPx
  TradeReportID IS NOT NULL
  AND Quantity IS NOT NULL
  AND Quantity > 0
  AND LastPx IS NOT NULL
  -- long side: Side = 'Buy' or 'Long' or 'B' (common conventions) — keep these conventions out of caller so literals are here.
  AND LOWER(side.Side) IN ('buy', 'long', 'b')
  -- ensure this side's OrderID matches the top-level OrderID when present, or accept when side.OrderID is NULL
  AND (side.OrderID IS NULL OR side.OrderID = t.OrderID)
valid_trades_long_side.description: Select the subset of rows that represent valid trades and are on the long side. Do not aggregate; keep one row per trade.

raw_trade_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID AS trade_id,
  TransactTime AS trade_timestamp,
  NULL AS algorithm,
  Symbol AS symbol,
  LastPx AS open_price,
  StrikePrice AS close_price,
  -- Derive trade_direction from the first element of Sides if present
  (SELECT AS VALUE s.Side FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS s LIMIT 1) AS trade_direction,
  -- trade_multiplier not present in source; expose NULL so it can be set outside the view
  NULL AS trade_multiplier,
  -- preserve natural row ordering tie-breaker using SendingTime and OrderID
  STRUCT(SendingTime AS sending_time, OrderID AS order_id, TradeReportID AS trade_report_id) AS source_row_order
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
raw_trade_rows.description: Select the raw rows from the provided trade capture report dataset with no additional filtering; keep all columns needed for output and for ordering/tie-breaking.

normalized_trade_fields.name: normalized_trade_fields
normalized_trade_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key carried through
  r.trade_id AS trade_id,
  -- canonicalized timestamp (keep as TIMESTAMP)
  SAFE_CAST(r.trade_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP) AS trade_timestamp_ts,
  -- algorithm as string
  CAST(r.algorithm AS STRING) AS algorithm_str,
  -- symbol
  CAST(r.symbol AS STRING) AS symbol_str,
  -- numeric open/close
  SAFE_CAST(r.open_price AS FLOAT64) AS open_price_num,
  SAFE_CAST(r.close_price AS FLOAT64) AS close_price_num,
  -- trade direction normalized to string
  CAST(r.trade_direction AS STRING) AS trade_direction_str,
  -- multiplier to integer (SAFE_CAST to avoid failures)
  SAFE_CAST(r.trade_multiplier AS INT64) AS trade_multiplier_int,
  -- preserve original source row order for stable ordering/tie-breaks
  r.source_row_order AS source_row_order
FROM
  `raw_trade_rows` AS r
normalized_trade_fields.description: Project and canonicalize/cast the selected raw trade fields into the required output types (string/timestamp/float/int) and produce a stable source ordering key used to break ties as provided by the dataset.

SELECT

  p.plot_state_code AS state_code,
  p.plot_state_code_name AS state_name,
  pop.evaluation_description AS evaluation_group,
  -- infer macroplot presence: use COND.PROP_BASIS or POP fields; population has adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot and for_subplot
  -- lift literals out of view: none used here
  -- is_macroplot: true when adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot is NOT NULL (heuristic)
  IF(pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot IS NOT NULL, TRUE, FALSE) AS is_macroplot,
  pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot AS macr_proportion,
  pop.area_used_to_calculate_all_expansion_factors AS subp_proportion,
  -- provide adjustment_factor as the macroplot adjustment if present else subplot adjustment
  COALESCE(pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot, pop.adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot) AS adjustment_factor,
  -- condition_status_code, reserved_status_code, site productivity class come from plot table (COND fields are in other tables; use available plot columns)
  p.sample_kind_code AS condition_status_code,
  p.plot_nonsampled_reason_code AS reserved_status_code,
  p.plot_design_code AS site_productivity_class_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.plot` AS p
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` AS pop
ON
  p.plot_sequence_number = pop.plot_sequence_number
  AND p.plot_state_code = pop.state_code
-- join to latest evaluation group per state: determine latest by evaluation_description's associated inventory years.
JOIN (
  SELECT
    state_code,
    evaluation_description,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state_code ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(report_year_name, r'([0-9]{4})$') AS INT64) DESC NULLS LAST) AS evalgroup_rank
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population`
  WHERE
    evaluation_description IS NOT NULL
) AS latest
ON pop.state_code = latest.state_code
AND pop.evaluation_description = latest.evaluation_description
WHERE
  latest.evalgroup_rank = 1
plots_latest_evalgroup_sel.description: Join the selected plots to the per-state latest-evaluation_group ranking and keep only plot rows whose evaluation_group is the latest for their state (evalgroup_rank = 1). This produces the set of plots per state limited to the single latest EXPCURR evaluation_group for that state.

postal_code_level_aggregates.name: postal_code_level_aggregates
postal_code_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name AS state_id,
  region_name AS postal_code,
  -- total buildings in the postal code (use percent_covered and count_qualified as available signals)
  -- Prefer counting qualified buildings when present; fall back to NULL-safe sum logic.
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(count_qualified) AS INT64) AS total_buildings_postal,
  -- avg_sunroof_coverage_postal: percent_covered is percentage (0-100?) stored as FLOAT64 per row.
  -- Interpret percent_covered as fraction if values appear between 0 and 1; keep as-is otherwise.
  -- To keep view literal-free, we compute the average of percent_covered normalized to [0,1] by dividing values >1 by 100.
  AVG(
    CASE
      WHEN percent_covered IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN percent_covered > 1 THEN percent_covered / 100.0
      ELSE percent_covered
    END
  ) AS avg_sunroof_coverage_postal,
  -- avg_suitable_fraction_postal: percent_qualified is percent of covered buildings suitable; normalize similarly.
  AVG(
    CASE
      WHEN percent_qualified IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN percent_qualified > 1 THEN percent_qualified / 100.0
      ELSE percent_qualified
    END
  ) AS avg_suitable_fraction_postal,
  -- sum of potential panel count: use number_of_panels_total when available, otherwise sum directional/flat fields
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(
    COALESCE(number_of_panels_total,
      -- sum directional + flat + median as a fallback (NULL-safe)
      COALESCE(number_of_panels_n,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_s,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_e,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_w,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_f,0)
    )
  ) AS INT64) AS sum_potential_panel_count_postal,
  -- sum potential kW capacity: prefer kw_total, else derive from panel counts assuming kw_median approximates per-building median (fallback to panels*0.25 if panels present)
  SUM(
    COALESCE(
      kw_total,
      -- derive from panel totals (panels * 0.25 kW per panel)
      COALESCE(number_of_panels_total, NULL)
        * 0.25,
      -- if no total panels, try sum of directional panels *0.25
      (COALESCE(number_of_panels_n,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_s,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_e,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_w,0) + COALESCE(number_of_panels_f,0))
        * 0.25
    )
  ) AS sum_potential_kw_capacity_postal,
  -- sum potential annual kWh: prefer yearly_sunlight_kwh_total else sum directional components
  SUM(
    COALESCE(
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_total,
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_n,
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_s,
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_e,
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_w,
      yearly_sunlight_kwh_f,
      -- as a last resort, approximate from kw capacity * yearly_sunlight_kwh_median (kWh/kw/yr)
      (COALESCE(kw_total, (COALESCE(number_of_panels_total,0) * 0.25)) * COALESCE(yearly_sunlight_kwh_median, 0))
    )
  ) AS sum_potential_annual_kwh_postal,
  -- sum potential annual CO2 offset: carbon_offset_metric_tons is per-region potential; sum across rows
  SUM(COALESCE(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0.0)) AS sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_postal,
  -- current solar-equipped buildings: sum of existing_installs_count
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(COALESCE(existing_installs_count, 0)) AS INT64) AS current_solar_buildings_postal
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
GROUP BY
  state_name,
  region_name
postal_code_level_aggregates.description: Aggregate building-level metrics up to the postal-code-by-state grain: count total buildings, average Project Sunroof coverage fraction (area covered / building area), average suitable fraction of that coverage, sum of potential panel count, sum of potential kW capacity, sum of potential energy generation, sum of potential CO2 offset, and count of current solar-equipped buildings.

census_tract_level_aggregates.name: census_tract_level_aggregates
census_tract_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name AS state_id,
  region_name AS census_tract_id,
  COUNT(1) AS total_buildings_tract,
  AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_sunroof_coverage_tract,
  AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_suitable_fraction_tract,
  SUM(COALESCE(number_of_panels_total, 0)) AS sum_potential_panel_count_tract,
  SUM(COALESCE(kw_total, 0)) AS sum_potential_kw_capacity_tract,
  SUM(COALESCE(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0)) AS sum_potential_annual_kwh_tract,
  SUM(COALESCE(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0)) AS sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_tract,
  SUM(COALESCE(existing_installs_count, 0)) AS current_solar_buildings_tract
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
GROUP BY
  state_name,
  region_name
census_tract_level_aggregates.description: Aggregate building-level metrics up to the census-tract-by-state grain: same set of aggregates as for postal-code level (counts, averages, and sums) but grouped by census tract and state.

state_level_summary_and_gap.name: state_level_summary_and_gap
state_level_summary_and_gap.body_sql:
-- state_level_summary_and_gap view body
SELECT
  state_id,
  source_geography_level,
  -- carry key/id columns
  SUM(total_buildings_state) AS total_buildings_state,
  -- weighted average of sunroof coverage using buildings as weights
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(total_buildings_state * avg_sunroof_coverage_state), NULLIF(SUM(total_buildings_state),0)) AS avg_sunroof_coverage_state,
  -- weighted average of suitable fraction using buildings as weights
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(total_buildings_state * avg_suitable_fraction_state), NULLIF(SUM(total_buildings_state),0)) AS avg_suitable_fraction_state,
  -- adjusted qualified buildings = total_buildings * avg_coverage * avg_suitable_fraction
  CAST(SUM(ROUND(total_buildings_state * avg_sunroof_coverage_state * avg_suitable_fraction_state)) AS INT64) AS adjusted_qualified_buildings_state,
  -- sums of potentials and current installs
  SUM(sum_potential_panel_count_state) AS sum_potential_panel_count_state,
  SUM(sum_potential_kw_capacity_state) AS sum_potential_kw_capacity_state,
  SUM(sum_potential_annual_kwh_state) AS sum_potential_annual_kwh_state,
  SUM(sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_state) AS sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_state,
  SUM(current_solar_buildings_state) AS current_solar_buildings_state,
  -- installation gap = adjusted qualified buildings minus current installs (no negative gaps)
  GREATEST(
    CAST(SUM(ROUND(total_buildings_state * avg_sunroof_coverage_state * avg_suitable_fraction_state)) AS INT64)
    - CAST(SUM(current_solar_buildings_state) AS INT64),
    0) AS installation_gap_state
FROM (
  -- derive state-level summaries from postal_code_level_aggregates
  SELECT
    state_id,
    'postal_code' AS source_geography_level,
    -- bring postal-level metrics forward as "state-level pieces" to be aggregated above
    total_buildings_postal AS total_buildings_state,
    avg_sunroof_coverage_postal AS avg_sunroof_coverage_state,
    avg_suitable_fraction_postal AS avg_suitable_fraction_state,
    sum_potential_panel_count_postal AS sum_potential_panel_count_state,
    sum_potential_kw_capacity_postal AS sum_potential_kw_capacity_state,
    sum_potential_annual_kwh_postal AS sum_potential_annual_kwh_state,
    sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_postal AS sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_state,
    current_solar_buildings_postal AS current_solar_buildings_state
  FROM `postal_code_level_aggregates`

  UNION ALL

  -- derive state-level summaries from census_tract_level_aggregates
  SELECT
    state_id,
    'census_tract' AS source_geography_level,
    total_buildings_tract AS total_buildings_state,
    avg_sunroof_coverage_tract AS avg_sunroof_coverage_state,
    avg_suitable_fraction_tract AS avg_suitable_fraction_state,
    sum_potential_panel_count_tract AS sum_potential_panel_count_state,
    sum_potential_kw_capacity_tract AS sum_potential_kw_capacity_state,
    sum_potential_annual_kwh_tract AS sum_potential_annual_kwh_state,
    sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_tract AS sum_potential_annual_co2_offset_state,
    current_solar_buildings_tract AS current_solar_buildings_state
  FROM `census_tract_level_aggregates`
)
GROUP BY
  state_id,
  source_geography_level
state_level_summary_and_gap.description: Roll up both postal-code and census-tract aggregates to state-level summaries and compute the installation gap per state: total qualified buildings adjusted by average coverage and suitability minus current installations. Produce separate state-level summaries derived from postal-code aggregation and from census-tract aggregation so comparison between levels is possible.
